jobs.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Overview

Saronic Technologies is seeking a Program Manager to own the execution and delivery of Marauder, our 180-foot Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) produced at our Franklin, LA shipyard. This is a flagship large-scale production program, and the Program Manager is accountable for its cost, schedule, scope, and customer outcomes from contract award through delivery and sustainment.

Marauder is built at production scale and fielded across a wide and evolving range of complex missions. The Program Manager must pair deep expertise in large-scale shipbuilding and rate production with an instinct for modular kits, payloads, and mission-package integration—understanding how a common hull is configured, re-configured, and sustained to meet diverse customer needs. This role owns the balance between production throughput and mission flexibility.

The Program Manager serves as the primary customer-facing owner of the program, partnering closely with the internal Saronic growth, engineering, production and quality teams. The right candidate brings the customer fluency to manage government stakeholders and contracts, the technical acumen to make technical decisions aligned to the customer needs and contract requirements, and the programmatic discipline to deliver a large, complex platform at scale.

Responsibilities

Program Ownership & Delivery

Own end-to-end execution of the Marauder program, holding accountability for cost, schedule, scope, and quality from award through delivery and sustainment.
Serve as a leader and owner of the customer contract, deliverables, milestones, CDRLs, and contractual obligations.
Build and maintain the integrated program plan, aligning productions scheduled, engineering milestones, and integration timelines to customer commitments.
Drive risk and opportunity management across the program, escalating and resolving issues that threaten cost, schedule, or performance.
Report program health, forecasts, and decisions to Saronic leadership and customer stakeholders.

Large-Scale Production Interface

Partner with the Franklin production team to plan and execute rate production of a 180-foot ASV, from long-lead procurement through hull construction, outfitting, and delivery.
Monitor build sequencing, work breakdown, and production milestones to protect throughput while meeting quality and acceptance criteria.
Monitor and mitigate production risks—supply chain, labor, tooling, and facility constraints—unique to large-vessel shipbuilding.
Coordinate with Quality and Production to ensure build configurations and acceptance events meet customer and contractual standards.

Kit & Mission Package Integration

Own the configuration strategy for Marauder across a variety of mission packages, kits, and payloads on a common production hull.
Partner with Mission Package Integration Managers to plan integration of bespoke and commercial-off-the-shelf kits into the production and delivery flow.
Balance production standardization against mission-driven variance, protecting throughput while enabling flexibility.
Ensure integration timelines, dependencies, and configuration baselines are reflected in the master program plan.
Capture mission-package lessons learned and feed them back into production and product roadmaps.

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as the primary point of contact for the customer, managing expectations, requirements, and relationships across the program lifecycle.
Elicit and clarify evolving mission needs, translating them into actionable program and technical direction.
Lead program reviews, delivery events, and technical exchanges with government stakeholders, operators, and evaluators.
Deliver clear, concise program updates and after-action reporting to leadership and customer audiences.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Direct and synchronize a cross-functional program team spanning Production, Engineering, Software, Mission Services, and Forward Deployed Engineering.
Partner with Technical Program Managers to align technical execution with programmatic commitments.
Make and defend tradeoff decisions across capability, schedule, cost, and risk.
Drive disciplined configuration management across vessels, kits, payloads, and software versions

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Naval Architecture, or a related technical field.
10+ years of experience in program management of large-scale production, shipbuilding, or complex defense development programs. Program Management experience of Unmanned Surface Vessels highly desirable.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interface confidently with technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated ownership of cost, schedule, and scope on programs of significant size and complexity.
Experience managing production at rate, including supply chain, build sequencing, and delivery of large or complex hardware systems highly desirable.
Proven ability to manage government or defense customers, contracts, and deliverables.
Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time.
Secret security clearance eligibility required, active preferred.

Key Competencies

Can own a large, complex program end-to-end while balancing production throughput against mission flexibility.
Can connect production and configuration decisions to overall program cost, schedule, and mission outcomes.
Can translate evolving customer requirements into disciplined, executable program plans.
Leadership of high-performing, cross-functional, and distributed teams.
Established track record of clear, consistent, and correct communications with peers, leaders, and external stakeholders.
Comfort guiding customers through ambiguous or evolving requirements and shaping actionable solutions.

Physical Demands

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Occasional standing and walking within the office
Manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment
Visual acuity to read screens, documents, and reports
Occasional reaching, bending, or stooping to access file drawers, cabinets, or office supplies
Lifting and carrying items up to 20 pounds occasionally (e.g., office supplies, packages)

Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

Generous PTO and Holidays

Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

401(k) plan with company match

Stock Options:
Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

Pet Insurance:
Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline

Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

Job Overview

Saronic Technologies is seeking a Program Manager of Mission Package Integration to lead the development, integration, and delivery of modules, kits, and mission packages onto Saronic’s growing portfolio of Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) programs.

The Mission Package Integrations PM is a technical executor focusing on bridging Saronic platforms with both bespoke and commercial off the shelf kits, modules, and payloads. This role focuses on supporting existing customer contracts, strategizing new product lines, and driving organic growth through Saronic and customer-derived mission packages.

This role partners closely with the Saronic Growth, Programs and Strategic Partnerships organizations. This role is also expected to embed directly into programs, customer engagements, partnerships, or internal initiatives to provide support and technical expertise.

Responsibilities

Technical Execution Leadership

Lead end-to-end technical execution for mission package integration on Saronic platforms, from design support through field deployment and sustainment.
Support complex payload and package integrations on Saronic’s 180ft Marauder, while also supporting Corsair and Mirage integration efforts.
Translate high-level requirements into actionable steps for engineering and operations teams, driving disciplined technical execution in ambiguous environments.

jobs.description:
About Us

One team. Global challenges. Infinite opportunities. At Viasat, we’re on a mission to deliver connections with the capacity to change the world. For more than 35 years, Viasat has helped shape how consumers, businesses, governments and militaries around the globe communicate. We’re looking for people who think big, act fearlessly, and create an inclusive environment that drives positive impact to join our team.

What You'll Do

Viasat combines experienced leadership, advanced technology, operational agility, and a strong culture of innovation to address the world’s most complex communications challenges. Through bold and differentiated business models, we leverage commercial technologies to rapidly deliver transformative Warfighter operational capabilities and continuously evolve those solutions to maintain advantage against emerging adversary threats.

We employ a customer‑centric approach to address complex challenges through innovative, scalable solutions delivered on accelerated timelines. Viasat’s Government Space and Mission Systems business area supports a diverse portfolio that includes RF and optical communications, advanced sensing payloads, and fully integrated space missions.

As a Program Manager, you will lead multiple, concurrent initiatives to develop and deliver state-of-the-art satellite communication solutions for space vehicles at all orbit regimes. The ideal candidate will build and maintain strong customer relationships, lead complex development efforts, ensure successful program execution through disciplined cost, schedule, and risk management, drive proposal activities, and champion continuous improvement.

Build and maintain customer relationships.

Support capture and business development activities by contributing to business model and capability roadmap development and leading all aspects of proposal development, including strategy, cost estimation, and program execution content.

What You'll Need

A minimum of ten (10) years of progressive professional experience in program management or project management roles of complex technical development programs.
Demonstrated experience in cost, schedule, and performance management using EVM, variance analysis, risk management, and program dashboards.
Experience managing supplier relationships throughout the subcontract management lifecycle, including Statement of Work (SOW) development, performance tracking, and risk/issue escalation.
Experience leading proposal development.
Proven ability to work independently to define and resolve complex problems, anticipate future program needs, and establish meaningful metrics to measure success.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and effectively to diverse stakeholders.
Experienced relationship builder with a demonstrated ability to build and lead cross functional teams.
Ability to mentor, supporting the development of others and the resolution of complex challenges.

U.S. citizenship is required ability to maintain an active United States Top Secret/SCI Clearance.
Willingness and ability to travel up to 20%.

What Will Help You On The Job

Active U.S. Government security clearance, with SSBI/SCI eligibility.
Program Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
Master’s degree in relevant engineering, science, or business discipline.
Experience with U.S. Government contracting and execution of development programs.
Ability to contribute as a thought leader in strategic development and process improvement.
Understanding of systems engineering, integration, production, or sustainment for defense systems.
Experience supporting fully integrated space mission development programs, including space vehicle, ground segment, and operations.
Experience supporting payload and/or electronics development for space systems.

jobs.description:

Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With more than 1,700+ team members, 1,500+ AI & data experts, and 100+ prime contracts, we deliver on a scale and with purpose.

Credence is a welcoming environment for those looking to grow and make a meaningful impact. We encourage employees to push boundaries and help solve critical, world-changing federal challenges.

Credence has an immediate opening for a Program Manager B-2 at the senior to support the B-2 Division who is responsible for the modernization, test, production, fielding and sustainment of B-2 aircraft and related systems.  The B-2 is a high demand, low density fleet that is 20+ years old, is undergoing numerous concurrent acquisitions to solve obsolescence issues, and delivers critical aerial denial/anti-access and nuclear capabilities at Wright Patterson AFB, OH.
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the duties listed below:

Apply knowledge and experience in acquisition program management policies and procedures to USAF systems, subsystems, and equipment procurement activities, post-award project/program management tasks, and acquisition programs throughout their life cycles
Apply a full range of acquisition program management policies and procedures to perform acquisition management activities in support of existing and future F/B Directorate aircraft programs and platforms
Support proposal reviews as assigned by the customer and assist in coordinating documentation across financial management, program management, contracting, configuration management, engineering, and logistics management functions
Assist in consolidating functional inputs into common documents and planning for the accomplishment of program milestones
Provide assistance in risk management, project management, process improvement, and logistics support, including participation in Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) and Product/Process Improvement Working Groups (PIWGs)
Collect programmatic inputs from acquisition programs throughout their life cycles, including research, development, production, test, acquisition, fielding, sustainment, and modernization of existing and advanced capabilities
Assist in performing non-voting advisory support for program source selections, determining program progress, and communicating recommendations orally and in writing to higher organizational management
Develop and coordinate responses to taskers related to internal and external program inquiries
Support warfighter Urgent Operational Needs (UON) and Joint Urgent Operational Needs (JUON) execution teams by recommending accelerated test concepts, minimum integration levels, and trade-offs among risk, schedule, performance, and cost
Produce or review program office products, including business case analyses, trade-off studies, acquisition and logistics estimates, requirements documents, acquisition strategies, and acquisition plans
Support program offices during Materiel Solution Analysis (MSA), Technology Maturation and Risk Reduction (TMRR), Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD), Production and Deployment, and Operations and Support (O&S) phases, including milestone activities
Assist in performing MSAs leading up to design reviews and support the development of draft documentation and presentation materials based on cost, schedule, and performance limits
Support strategic scheduling and planning documentation, including Integrated Master Plans (IMPs), Integrated Master Schedules (IMSs), and reporting frameworks for event-based activities
Develop, analyze, and maintain integrated program schedules from concept exploration through system fielding, including lower-tier schedule networking, network statusing, duration assignments, relationship development, and schedule graphics
Evaluate contractor-proposed schedules against Government schedules, assess program office schedules against schedule databases, and support probabilistic and deterministic schedule risk assessments, including Schedule Risk Assessments (SRAs) using Monte Carlo simulation-based tools
Develop program management strategies and support Business Case Analyses (BCAs), Cost of Ownership (COO) analyses, aging aircraft analyses, process documentation, PWSs, SOWs, Data Item Descriptions (DIDs), test plans, acquisition plans, LCMPs, LCSPs, ELMPs, QASPs, ASPs, IMPs, IMSs, AIPs, and AIMPs
Support development of contract strategies, Work Breakdown Structures (WBSs), program risk assessments, market survey requirements, executive briefings, stakeholder coordination, briefing updates, and meeting minutes
Perform analyses to support program strategy decisions and courses of action and provide program assessments to ensure milestone documentation aligns with program strategy
Provide inputs, draft, coordinate, adjudicate comments, and produce final coordinated milestone documents and assessments, including staff summary packages for milestone approval
Support requirements document development and the Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System (JCIDS) process and staffing
Translate user requirements documents, including Capability Development Documents (CDDs), Capability Production Documents (CPDs), and CONOPs, into Request for Proposal (RFP) documentation for the F/B Directorate
Support key acquisition events and reviews, including SRRs, PDRs, CDRs, TRRs, TCMs, FCAs, PCAs, PRRs, TIMs, and other applicable reviews
Apply program management initiatives involving commercial items, including Non-Developmental Items (NDI), Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS), and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)-certified items
Support commercial practices and acquisition approaches such as Performance Based Business Environment (PBBE), Evolutionary Acquisition (EA), Agile Acquisition (AA), JCIDS, CONOPS, partnering, architectural views, and Capabilities Review and Risk Assessment (CRRA)
Assist with Automated Business Services System (ABSS), System Management Analysis Reporting Tool (SMART), and Integrated Budget Documentation and Execution System (IDECS), including producing documents using IDECS
Support DAG processes, including Monthly Acquisition Reports (MARs), Defense Acquisition Executive Summary (DAES), Selected Acquisition Reports (SARs), and the Task Management Tool (TMT)
Plan, coordinate, and participate in integrated program reviews and conferences, including executive, readiness, technical, budget, design, weapon system, requirements working group, supportability, and management reviews
Review and analyze weapon system prime and subcontractor Earned Value Management (EVM) systems and support management of the action item process following program reviews
Support program briefings and reports by gathering information, preparing charts, presenting briefings, and providing other program support as needed
Process and complete Modification Proposal AF Form 1067 activities, including logging, assigning review responsibilities, tracking completions, providing responses to using commands, and archiving results
Provide programmatic support for using commands' Requirements and Planning Councils (R&PCs) or similar requirements review processes
Support capability planning and development actions, including implementation of policies, processes, and tools, High Powered Team (HPT) support, and capability-based planning processes for AFMC
Support AFMC Capabilities Integration Panel resources, including financial and manpower resources, and review capability requirements and option sets to ensure interoperability and linkages to other capabilities
Communicate across multiple platforms, programs, phases, and enterprises while supporting integration of intelligence information and infrastructure for cross-enterprise capabilities planning and system acquisition
Support establishment of a capability architect function to develop integrated architectures for cross-enterprise comparison, analysis, and integration
Identify and advocate AF Operational Support (OS) capability requirements and support OS transformation through capability-based planning, modernization initiatives, process engineering, and integration of intelligence from concept development through sustainment
Promote the use of Modeling, Simulation, and Analysis (MS&A) throughout the acquisition life cycle and support development and maintenance of common-use MS&A tools
Support command leadership and policy for modeling, simulation, and analysis to enable capability-based planning and acquisition; access modeling databases and perform specific analysis
Plan, organize, and manage critical aspects of the development, production, and/or deployment of capabilities, including systems of systems, families of systems, systems, subsystems, and equipment
Support the Directorate/Division Self-Inspection Program (SIP), including preparing for inspections, distributing checklist information, developing and maintaining checklist tracking/reporting, monitoring completion status, and recommending corrective actions
Prepare, maintain, update, and review test and test-related documentation, including the Test and Evaluation Master Plan (TEMP), Integrated System Test Plan, Integrated Test Team (ITT) Charter, Program Introduction Document (PID), Statement of Capabilities (SOC), and other required test plans and reports
Review test documentation for adequacy, specification/performance requirement compliance, and conformity with mandatory guidance, and provide recommendations for improvement
Recommend, assess, and analyze requirements and objectives, test and evaluation concepts, strategies, and plans
Coordinate acceptance test procedures and associated plans, including testing requirements with program office customers, contractors, and other agencies with standardization requirements for test programs

Requirements

Education, Requirements and Qualifications:

Must have a Secret clearance

jobs.description:
IAM RBAC Lead

Marsh McLennan is seeking an experienced and strategic IAM RBAC Lead to establish and lead the enterprise-wide Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) strategy, framework, and operating model.

This is a global leadership role that will play a key part in strengthening access governance, improving operational efficiency, and supporting secure, scalable identity and access management across the organization.

What can you expect:

A senior leadership role with global scope and high visibility across IAM, Security, HR, Technology, and business teams.
The opportunity to shape and mature Marsh McLennan’s enterprise RBAC framework and operating model.
A collaborative environment where you will partner with stakeholders to drive access governance, improve service quality, and support business transformation.
The chance to work on innovative initiatives, including AI and automation, to improve RBAC processes and operational excellence.
A role that combines strategy, leadership, and hands-on delivery within a complex enterprise environment.

We will count on you to:

Lead the enterprise RBAC program across multiple business units and regions.
Define and deliver the RBAC strategy, roadmap, standards, and operating model.
Build strong partnerships with business, technology, IAM, security, and HR stakeholders to gather requirements and define role ownership.
Oversee role design, role lifecycle management, access certification, and governance processes.
Improve service quality by reducing provisioning errors, policy exceptions, and operational risk.
Monitor RBAC performance through dashboards, KPIs, KRIs, and reporting to leadership.
Drive continuous improvement, maturity assessments, and implementation of best practices.
Support SDLC integration, change management, compliance, and post-production support.
Lead and develop a regional team of employees and consultants.

What you need to have:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
5+ years of experience leading enterprise RBAC or IAM transformation initiatives.
Strong experience with identity governance platforms such as SailPoint Identity Security Cloud / IdentityIQ.
Solid understanding of RBAC, identity governance, provisioning, authorization, and access management.
Proven leadership, stakeholder management, communication, and presentation skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making skills.
Experience working with enterprise processes, standards, SDLC, and implementation lifecycle support.
Knowledge of security and compliance frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, and GDPR.

What makes you stand out:

Experience leading RBAC design in a large, complex, global organization.
A strong track record of building and maturing enterprise IAM operating models.
Confidence working across business and technical teams to influence decisions and drive adoption.
Experience using data, dashboards, and metrics to improve operational performance.
Familiarity with AI, automation, and innovation in IAM or access governance.
Experience managing teams and coordinating delivery across multiple stakeholders and projects.
A proactive, collaborative approach with the ability to simplify complexity and deliver results.

About BAE Systems

Recognized annually as a Top Workplace in Utah consecutively since 2018, employees at BAE Systems enjoy an exceptional work culture, employment stability, growth opportunities, and job satisfaction knowing they are helping to protect the country through the development of the most technological advancements in our nation’s history. Air and Space Force Solutions, a business unit within BAE Systems, has an opening at our Hill Air Force Base, Utah location for an experienced Lead Cybersecurity Analyst. Develop cybersecurity documentation and conduct peer reviews

jobs.description:
Build your best future with the Johnson Controls team. As a global leader in smart, healthy, and sustainable buildings, we help improve the performance of buildings to serve people, places, and the planet. At Johnson Controls, you will join a collaborative team with opportunities to grow through meaningful work, learning, and hands-on project experience.

Role Overview

As a Fire Project Manager, you will lead complex fire alarm, security, and communications installation projects across commercial, educational, healthcare, industrial, and military environments. You will be responsible for planning and executing projects that are delivered safely, on time, within scope, and with a strong focus on customer satisfaction, quality, and financial performance.

Key Responsibilities

Lead fire alarm, security, and communications installation projects from initiation through closeout.
Set up local project offices and coordinate scope definition, risk identification, project methodology, and resource allocation.
Manage project schedules, costs, safety, quality, and customer expectations throughout the project lifecycle.
Coordinate the flow of work from design and permitting through material delivery, labor scheduling, and field installation.
Facilitate project reviews, including Work in Progress meetings, status updates, and resolution of project issues.
Support change order processing and work to improve project margin on each assignment.
Ensure projects are completed on time, within scope, and in alignment with company standards and customer requirements.

Stay close to the work by coordinating design, permits, delivery, labor, and installation details so obstacles are identified and removed early.
Use a disciplined project plan to track schedule, budget, quality, and risk, and communicate progress clearly to internal teams and customers.
Improve every day by following published codes, standards, unique specifications, and AHJ requirements with candor and practical problem-solving.
Win as one team by working across field, office, and customer stakeholders to resolve issues, manage change orders, and deliver strong project results.
Follow departmental and SOX procedures, and maintain accurate project documentation from start to finish.

High school diploma or equivalent.
5 years of installation experience in Fire, Electrical, or Security systems.
Project Management Professional certification to be obtained within two years of employment.
NICET Level II to be obtained within one year of employment.
Proficiency in MS Office applications, including Excel and Project.
Ability to create Excel spreadsheets, reference data in other spreadsheets, and create macros.
Availability for frequent local travel.

Certificate or diploma in Fire & Life Safety, Electrical/Electronic, or Security.
Certification in Fire Alarm Systems.

We offer a competitive salary and bonus plan, with a hiring range of $86,000 to $105,000, based on experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. You will also be eligible for a comprehensive benefits package including 401K, medical, dental, and vision care, available day one. Additional support includes paid vacation, holidays, and sick time, extensive product and on-the-job cross-training opportunities, a collaborative environment, a company vehicle, and our Zero Harm commitment to safety.

If you are ready to lead important projects and make a meaningful impact, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Network Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Key Responsibilities

People Management & Team Development

Directly manage a team of Network Implementation Engineers across project delivery lifecycle; set clear performance expectations, conduct structured 1:1s, and own individual development plans.
Build a culture of execution discipline — ticket hygiene, change management compliance, documentation quality, and rigorous project close-out.
Identify skill gaps and build structured training and certification pathways aligned to ECI’s service portfolio.
Manage performance formally and informally; address issues directly, constructively, and on record when required.
Participate in hiring decisions for the implementation function, including technical assessments and structured panel interviews.

Project Delivery & Program Management

Own end-to-end delivery of network implementation projects spanning new client onboarding, infrastructure refreshes, office builds, and technology migrations.
Define and enforce project intake, scoping, scheduling, and resource allocation standards across the team.
Maintain active visibility across all open workstreams; surface and resolve blockers before they become client escalations.
Drive post-implementation reviews and root cause analysis; translate findings into repeatable process improvements for the team.
Coordinate with Client Services, Solutions Architecture, and pre-sales to align implementation timelines with client commitments and ECI delivery standards.

Technical Standards & Oversight

Serve as the technical authority for ECI’s implementation standards covering Cisco (Catalyst, Nexus, IOS-XE/XR), Palo Alto firewalls, Meraki, and SD-WAN platforms.
Review and approve low-level designs (LLDs) and implementation runbooks before execution.
Establish and enforce configuration standards that ensure consistency, repeatability, and alignment with client security and compliance requirements (SOC 2, PCI-DSS, NIST, HIPAA).
Serve as escalation point for complex in-flight technical issues; engage hands-on when warranted while ensuring the team learns from every resolution.
Champion Zero Trust and SASE architecture principles within ECI’s implementation workflows.

Client & Stakeholder Communication

Own implementation status communication to client stakeholders; translate technical risk into clear business impact language.
Represent the implementation team in internal delivery reviews, capacity planning, and service improvement forums.
Maintain ECI’s documentation standard across implementation plans, network diagrams, as-built records, and configuration baselines — ensuring clean handoffs to managed services teams.

Qualifications

Required

10+ years of progressive network engineering experience with a demonstrable track record in enterprise implementation, ideally within an MSP or multi-client environment.
3+ years of direct people management — you have hired engineers, set goals, handled performance, and actively developed talent.
Deep technical proficiency in Cisco networking (Catalyst, Nexus, IOS-XE/XR), Palo Alto firewalls (App-ID, Threat Prevention, VPN, Panorama), and wireless (WLC, Meraki MR/MS/MX).
Strong working knowledge of routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, EIGRP), VLANs, QoS, and IPv4/IPv6 fundamentals.
Proven ability to run multiple concurrent implementation projects with accountability for schedules, resources, and stakeholder communication.
Solid understanding of security frameworks, compliance standards, and change management governance in regulated client environments.

Preferred

Active CCNP, CCIE, or PCNSE certification; equivalent demonstrated expertise considered.
Experience with SD-WAN (Cisco Viptela, VeloCloud) and SASE / Zero Trust architecture in client deployments.
Familiarity with automation tooling (Python, Ansible) to drive repeatability and reduce manual effort across the team.
Experience with network monitoring platforms (SolarWinds, PRTG, Meraki Insights) and using telemetry data to drive delivery quality.
Hedge fund, financial services, or similarly regulated client-facing environment experience is a strong plus.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field — or equivalent professional experience.

Who We Are Looking For

Beyond credentials, we are hiring for a specific leadership profile. The right candidate:

Communicates expectations without ambiguity and follows through consistently. Leads with clarity.
Engineers respect them because they know the stack — not just the title. Commands technical credibility.
Holds the team and themselves to high execution standards without micromanaging. Drives accountability.
Focused on delivery quality and reliability, not just activity volume. Solves for client outcomes.
Understands the job is to build the best team — not to be the best individual engineer on it. Scales through people.

ECI’s culture is all about connection -
connection with our clients, our technology and most importantly with each other. In addition to working with an amazing team around the world, ECI also offers a competitive compensation package and the range for this role is a maximum of $142,000 annually with flexible PTO, health benefit eligibility the first of the month, life insurance, pet insurance, 401K and so much more! If you believe you’d be a great fit and are ready for your best job ever, we’d like to hear from you!!

Love Your Job, Share Your Technology Passion, Create Your Future Here!

Job Description

Description reviewed 08/18/26

Basic Purpose

Positions in this job family are assigned responsibility involving the coordination, supervision and direction of a correctional security program in a state adult correctional facility.

Typical Functions

Coordinates and supervises or directs correctional security functions and activities at an adult correctional facility; may serve as a shift supervisor with responsibility for all assigned units and functions in a large facility or as the chief of security in a smaller facility.
May serve as commander of a correctional emergency response team; schedules training exercises and coordinates activities.
Conducts special investigations, particularly concerning incidents that occur during assigned shifts.
Coordinates and supervises security, riot and escape procedures, including procedures for inmate counts and searches for escape materials and contraband.
Prepares daily work schedules for security personnel; prepares and maintains appropriate records concerning employees and residents.
Conducts inspections of assigned staff at beginning of shift to assure proper attire and fitness for duty; makes periodic inspections of posts to assure that they are properly maintained; prepares administrative reports concerning the operation of the shift.
Acts as liaison to local law enforcement agencies; provides information and file changes; arranges court appearances.
Serves as member of the administrative institutional staff; participates in the formulation of institutional policies, rules and regulations.

Level Descriptor

At this level employees serve as a correctional security captain with overall responsibility for the operations of an assigned shift within a medium or maximum-security facility and supervision of staff.

Responsibilities may involve ensuring the proper functioning of the electronic, mechanical, surveillance, and physical security systems; overseeing physical and sanitary conditions, special investigations, and adherence to operational and policy protocols; directing the correctional emergency response team; and assumption of the operation and management of the facility after normal business hours or in the absence of the warden.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, And Competencies

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities required at this level include knowledge of supervisory methods and techniques; of staffing patterns and scheduling the distribution of staff and work assignments; of methods and objectives of discipline required for inmates under restraint; of the psychology of inmate behavior; of the use and care of firearms; of proper restraint methods and techniques; of the fundamentals of English usage; of basic math; of report writing techniques; and of the modern practices of prison management

and the treatment of inmates.

Ability is required to establish and maintain effective working relationships; to follow oral and written instructions; to gather and organize facts and complete clear, concise reports; to quickly evaluate a situation and adopt an effective course of action; to exercise alertness and be able to act quickly in an emergency; to effectively communicate security techniques; to maintain proficiency in firearms; to assess and manage conflict resolutions within the inmate population; and to direct and supervise the work of others.

Education And Experience

Education and Experience requirements at this level consist of four years of experience in correctional or security work for a government agency or private corrections agency and the following statutory requirements of Title 57, O.S. Section 510: a. The minimum age for service shall be twenty (20) years of age. The Director shall have the authority to establish the maximum age for correctional officers entering service and b. possession of thirty (30) semester hours from an accredited college or university; or possession of a high school diploma acquired from an accredited high school or GED equivalent testing program and graduation from a training course conducted by or approved by the Department and certified by the Council on Law Enforcement Education and Training either prior to employment or during the first six (6) months of employment.

Note: Successful completion of the GED test is based upon standards established by the Oklahoma Department of Education.

Special Requirements

Per 57 O.S. 510 applicants/employees in this job family shall be subject to the following additional requirements: (a) be of good moral character; (b) before going on duty alone, satisfactory completion of an adequate training program for correctional officers and guards, as prescribed and approved by the State Board of Corrections; and (c) satisfactory completion of a physical in keeping with the conditions of the job description on an annual basis and along the guidelines as established by the Department of Corrections.

Applicants must possess a valid driver’s license at the time of appointment in order to perform necessary travel.

Applicants will be subject to drug testing.

Applicants must be willing and able to work any assigned shift or day of the week.

NOTE: Employees in this job classification may be designated as peace officers by the Director and required to meet the training and screening requirements conducted by the Department and certified by the Council on Law Enforcement Education and Training. (57 O.S. 510)

No person who has received a verdict of guilty or pled guilty or nolo contendere to any offense required to register pursuant to the Sex Offenders Registration Act is eligible for employment as a peace officer. (57 O.S. 589.C)

No person who has been convicted of a crime of moral turpitude who has not received a full pardon from the proper agency is eligible for employment as a peace officer. (70 O.S. 3311)

No person who has been convicted of a nonviolent felony and who has not received a full pardon from the proper authority, or who has been convicted of any other felony offense, is eligible for employment in this job classification. (21 O.S. 1283.B)

No person who has been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence, who has not been pardoned for, or had the conviction expunged or set aside, or is subject to a court order that restrains the person from harassing, stalking, or threatening an intimate partner or the partners’ child or engaging in other conduct that would place an intimate partner or the partners’ child in reasonable fear of bodily injury

and includes a finding that the person is a credible threat; or who has been dishonorably discharged from any branch of the armed services is eligible for employment in this job classification. (18 U.S.C. 922)

The Department of Corrections has determined that some positions in this job family are safety sensitive as defined by63 O.S.

427.8.

jobs.description:
About AlphaSense

The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content.

The acquisition of Tegus by AlphaSense in 2024 advances our shared mission to empower professionals to make smarter decisions through AI-driven market intelligence. Together, AlphaSense and Tegus will accelerate growth, innovation, and content expansion, with complementary product and content capabilities that enable users to unearth even more comprehensive insights from thousands of content sets. Our platform is trusted by over 6,000 enterprise customers, including a majority of the S&P 500. Founded in 2011, AlphaSense is headquartered in New York City with more than 2,000 employees across the globe and offices in the U.S., U.K., Finland, India, Singapore, Canada, and Ireland. Come join us!

Remote within Canada, able to work in the Pacific time zone

About The Role

We are hiring Security Operations Analyst II
to join our Security Operations team in a fully remote capacity from Canada. This role sits at Tier 1–2 in our operating model — you are past the stage of learning what alerts look like and ready to own triage, perform structured investigations, and contribute to detection quality. You will handle the day-to-day alert queue, investigate escalated or ambiguous cases, handle incidents and work closely with senior analysts and the Security Operations Manager to close coverage gaps.

We expect you to think analytically, document thoroughly, and operate with growing independence. You will be supported by experienced colleagues and a mature toolset, but you are expected to bring real investigative instinct and a curiosity to grow to the role from day one.

What You Will Do

Alert Triage & Investigation

Monitor and triage alerts across endpoint, network, cloud, runtime and identity data sources with accuracy and appropriate urgency
Perform structured investigations on escalated or ambiguous alerts: pivot across log sources, correlate events, and build a coherent timeline
Classify alerts correctly — true positive, false positive, or benign — with documented rationale, not just a verdict
Identify scope and blast radius on confirmed incidents: affected users, systems, and data before escalating or containing
Escalate to senior analysts with a complete investigation package — context, evidence, timeline, and a hypothesis

Incident Response Support

Participate in active incident response under senior analyst or manager direction: evidence collection, log pulls, timeline reconstruction
Execute containment actions — endpoint isolation, account suspension, token revocation — as directed with documented rationale
Maintain accurate and timely case documentation throughout the incident lifecycle
Contribute to post-incident timelines and assist with root cause documentation

Cloud & Identity Security Monitoring

Monitor cloud audit logs and native threat detection findings for suspicious IAM activity, unusual API calls, and access anomalies
Investigate identity provider events: suspicious logins, MFA bypass attempts, session anomalies, and unauthorized app assignments
Recognize common cloud-native attack patterns: credential abuse via metadata service, privilege escalation via IAM role assumption, and storage misconfiguration access
Correlate cloud-side events with endpoint and network telemetry to build a fuller picture of attacker activity

Detection & Quality Improvement

Flag false positives and noisy detections with enough context for a senior analyst or detection engineer to tune them
Identify gaps in existing detection coverage based on alert patterns you observe during triage
Apply knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK to label attacker techniques and communicate findings consistently
Contribute to runbook accuracy by flagging outdated steps or missing guidance encountered during investigations
Participate with Detections Engineers to build detections and contribute to automating activity with an Engineering mindset

Documentation & Communication

Write clear, concise case notes that a colleague could pick up mid-investigation without needing to re-investigate from scratch
Produce shift handoff summaries that accurately represent open cases, pending actions, and investigation status
Communicate incident updates to the Security Operations Manager with sufficient clarity to brief upward without re-investigation

Required

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

2–4+ years of hands-on experience in a SOC, or security operations role with direct alert triage responsibility
Solid understanding of the MITRE ATT&CK framework — you use it to label and communicate attacker behavior, not just reference it
Working knowledge of EDR tooling: process tree analysis, behavioral detection review, and basic endpoint artifact interpretation
Familiarity with SIEM-based investigation: querying logs, correlating events across sources, and building timelines from normalized data
Understanding of foundational network protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, TLS) and how attackers abuse them
Exposure to cloud security monitoring ex. AWS or GCP — including audit log review and IAM-related alert investigation
Experience investigating identity-based alerts in an enterprise identity provider (e.g., Okta, Entra ID, or equivalent)
Strong written communication: your case notes are accurate, structured, and useful to someone who wasn’t there

Preferred

Experience with next-gen EDR platforms (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne, or equivalent) beyond basic alert review — RTR, process trees, custom detections
Hands-on SIEM experience with a cloud-native platform (e.g., Google SecOps/Chronicle, Microsoft Sentinel, or equivalent)
Exposure to CSPM or cloud security tooling (e.g., Wiz, Prisma Cloud, or equivalent) as an investigation data source
Familiarity with AWS IR fundamentals: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, VPC Flow Logs, IAM chain analysis
Understanding of encoding vs. encryption vs. hashing and their relevance to attacker obfuscation techniques
Experience working alongside or receiving escalations from a managed detection and response (MDR) partner
Relevant certifications: CompTIA CySA+, Security+, BTL1, GCIH, or equivalent practical security credential

jobs.title: Principal, Strategy and Operations Manager - GBSG U.S. Marketing
jobs.description:
Overview

Intuit is a mission-driven, global financial platform company that gives everyone the opportunity to prosper. We do this by using technology to solve our customers’ most important problems. We serve customers by finding more ways to put more money in their pockets, eliminating work and drudgery so they can focus on their lives and what matters to them, and ensuring that every financial decision that they make, they make it with confidence. We are also at an important point in Intuit’s transformation, as AI and human intelligence reshape both the experiences we deliver for customers and how we operate. Across GBSG, that means making sharper choices about where we invest, how we grow, and how we move with greater speed and focus.

As a Principal Strategy and Operations Manager, you will sit at the center of Commercial Operations, the connective tissue between strategy and execution across the commercial organization. You'll own the planning rhythm, drive the initiatives that unlock growth and profitability, and turn ambiguous business problems into decisions leadership can act on. Working at the intersection of business strategy, data analysis, and AI-enabled operations, you'll partner closely with finance, marketing, sales, and product to translate priorities into measurable outcomes and to build the operating cadence that keeps them on track. Be part of a high-growth environment where your contributions have direct, visible impact. We are looking for a strategic operator who is an avid learner, experimenter, and builder, ready to rewire how Commercial Operations runs in the AI era.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning and Execution: Develop and execute key business initiatives to drive growth and profitability. Own and evolve the quarterly and annual planning process, helping leaders make explicit choices about priorities, investments, tradeoffs and sequencing. Use AI-assisted tools to compress cycle time and get to decisions faster.
Project Management and Cross-functional Collaboration: Manage strategic initiatives from conception to execution, collaborating with finance, marketing, sales, and product teams to ensure alignment and effective implementation. Identify and drive mitigation strategies, prioritize initiatives, and ensure alignment with cross-functional leaders to assess effectiveness and make necessary adjustments.
Performance and Data Analysis: Identify and recommend improvements to processes and systems, conducting in-depth analyses of business performance, market trends, and operational metrics to enhance efficiency and inform strategic decisions. Use AI and automation to expand the scope and speed of analysis, and to automate recurring reporting so effort shifts from data assembly to insight.
Executive Communication: Shape executive decisions by distilling complex analysis and data into clear recommendations, alternatives, and tradeoffs. Communicate those insights through crisp presentations, written narratives, and other executive-ready materials that create the clarity and alignment leaders need to make decisions and move.
AI Enablement and Velocity: Bring a demonstrated track record of using AI to meaningfully increase personal and team throughput. Design changes that address root causes rather than adding another process or layer.

Qualifications

This role demands a blend of analytical prowess, operational expertise, and leadership skills to drive effective business strategies and operational efficiencies in a complex and evolving environment.

7+ years of experience in strategy consulting, business operations, or a related field, ideally with experience in management consulting or large technology companies.
Experience leading multi-year strategy and planning, including long-range planning, annual planning, scenario development, and translating strategy into operating priorities.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience in data analysis, financial modeling, and KPI trend analysis. Proficiency in SQL, Python or similar for data analysis and automation scripting; experience with no‑code/low‑code platforms (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code); a plus.
Track record of working cross‑functionally with product, engineering, data scientists, and marketing channel owners. Understanding of marketing measurement, incrementality testing, and performance metrics.
Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills. Ability to develop clear and impactful reports and presentations for stakeholders. Demonstrated leadership abilities with experience influencing and building partnerships across all levels of an organization.
Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, with strong organizational and time management skills. Comfortable working in a dynamic, high-growth environment with ambiguity.
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Finance, Engineering, Economics, Business, or a related field; advanced degree such as an MBA preferred.

Footer

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

The Expected Base Pay Range For This Position Is

Mountain View $197,000 - $266,000

New York $190,000- $257,000

San Diego, CA $196,000- $265,000

jobs.title: SNAP Program Manager
jobs.description:
Under the general direction of the Senior Program Manager of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Programs or designee, the SNAP Program Manager provides leadership and operational oversight of the SNAP Employment and Training (known in Massachusetts as SNAP Path to Work) team within ForHealth Consulting. This role is responsible for managing staff and coordinating SNAP team activities, including partner recruitment and training, budget development, federal and state claiming processes, performance monitoring, and general departmental operations. The position is tasked with leading initiatives that advance ForHealth Consultings SNAP portfolio.

The successful candidate for this position will demonstrate operational management expertise, a strong aptitude for creative problem-solving, a commitment to implementing process improvements and innovative practices, and a comfort level with budgeting and financial decision-making. Exceptional organizational and leadership skills are essential, as the SNAP program manager must handle multiple assignments with minimal supervision and effectively collaborate with diverse internal and external partners. This position may require occasional travel to locations within Massachusetts and elsewhere in New England.

The Access and Eligibility Services (AES) group is part of ForHealth Consulting, a division of UMass Chan Medical School. AES supports critical state and federal public assistance programs on behalf of the Massachusetts Department of Transitional Assistance (DTA) to help hundreds of thousands of low-income individuals in Massachusetts with food and shelter expenses. ForHealth Consulting contracts with community organizations and agencies who provide services to DTA SNAP clients and applicants. SNAP Path to Work is a program that connects SNAP clients in Massachusetts with community providers of job skills training programs and employment preparation. The SNAP team at ForHealth Consulting assists DTAs SNAP community partners to obtain federal dollars for eligible services under the SNAP Path to Work and Outreach programs by identifying allowable activities and funding streams, offering training and technical assistance, reviewing quarterly claims, and disbursing federal reimbursements.

Responsibilities

Provide supplemental support to the SNAP Senior Program Manager; manage general operations of the unit to meet client goals and expectations. Ensure appropriate staffing levels and timely completion of all projects and tasks.
Oversee and manage staff activities related to preparing and completing federal claims and monitoring contracted partners. Review claims for accuracy and compliance and/or authorize claims for submission.
Manage the work of the SNAP team to complete annual partner reviews and audits, including partner budget reviews.
Assist in preparing operational budgets for the SNAP unit.
Help develop, implement, and recommend improvements to SNAP programs to expand the partner base, increase federal claiming, and optimize outcomes for community partners. Develop and implement procedures and guidelines to accomplish project objectives and goals efficiently.
Ensure that all activities of the SNAP unit and its policies and procedures for partners are compliant with applicable state and federal rules and regulations.
Lead strategic recruitment efforts of new partners to address community and client needs.
Collaborate with staff and support units to ensure timely and accurate financial reconciliation for SNAP-related activities.
Manage staff and conduct annual performance reviews to ensure alignment with organizational goals and to foster individual growth and professional development.
Foster a culture of innovation and continuous improvement among SNAP staff through regular meetings, ongoing awareness and support for new ideas.
Represent the department in a professional capacity with internal management, contracted partners, DTA leadership, and other government agencies.
Participate in the broader AES team and support its programs and projects where necessary.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Finance, Fiscal Management, or a related field, or two years of relevant professional experience in lieu of the degree.
Demonstrated strong experience in supervision with the ability to manage and motivate staff
Proficiency in computer-based tools, including spreadsheets and word processing software (MS Office Suite)

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of state and federal regulations as they apply to public assistance programs
Understanding of SNAP regulations related to SNAP Employment and Training (SNAP Path to Work), strongly preferred
Knowledge of United States Department of Agriculture Food and Nutrition Administration (USDA FNA) programs and/or experience working with the advocate community on nutrition and anti-hunger projects
Experience in financial or operational management, including fiscal responsibility and decision-making
Strong oral and written communication skills

The University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School welcomes all qualified applicants and complies with all state and federal anti-discrimination laws.

jobs.description:

Good people. Dedicated People. Hard-working people.

CompTech is a service-oriented program management and technical company working to build lasting relationships with small and large companies, municipalities, and Government agencies. Headquartered in Dayton, OH, our clients nationwide are provided with services in client-focused practice areas resulting in solutions to organizational challenges.

Job Description

Job Title: Program Manager

Location: Dayton, OH (Hybrid) or Remote (based on business needs)

Must have experience managing Federal Government programs, contracts or large technical projects and have working knowledge of Federal Government Contracts**

As a growing Federal contractor, CompTech values leaders who are willing to roll up their sleeves and contribute wherever needed. In addition to overseeing program execution, the Program Manager partners with executive leadership to support business development, operational improvements, quality initiatives, and strategic growth efforts. The successful candidate is equally comfortable leading customer programs, mentoring teams, solving operational challenges, and supporting the company's continued expansion.

Overview

CompTech is seeking an experienced Program Manager to lead the successful execution of Federal Government programs and internal strategic initiatives. The Program Manager serves as the primary operational lead responsible for delivering exceptional customer service, ensuring contract performance, managing cross-functional teams, and driving projects and programs to successful completion.

Reporting directly to executive leadership, this individual will oversee program execution from planning through delivery, ensuring performance, quality, schedule, budget, and customer satisfaction objectives are consistently achieved. The ideal candidate is an experienced leader with a strong understanding of Federal Government contracting, operational excellence, and continuous process improvement.

Program Leadership

Provide overall leadership and management for assigned Federal Government contracts and internal strategic initiatives.
Develop and execute program management plans, project schedules, staffing strategies, budgets, and performance metrics.
Ensure programs are delivered on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with contractual requirements and customer expectations.
Lead cross-functional teams while fostering collaboration, accountability, and operational excellence.
Monitor program performance, identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and proactively resolve issues impacting cost, schedule, or performance.
Present program status, key performance indicators, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and customers.

Customer & Contract Management

Serve as the primary point of contact between CompTech, Government customers, subcontractors, vendors, and internal stakeholders.
Build and maintain strong customer relationships through responsive communication and exceptional program execution.
Support contract startup, transition activities, contract modifications, option years, and program closeout.
Ensure full compliance with contract requirements, Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), company policies, and applicable Government standards.
Coordinate with subcontractors and vendors to ensure successful delivery of contractual requirements.

Operations & Business Support

Partner with Business Development to support proposal development, staffing plans, transition strategies, technical volumes, and Requests for Proposal (RFP) responses.
Collaborate with Recruiting to identify, interview, and onboard qualified personnel for funded and anticipated contract positions.
Support company strategic initiatives, operational improvements, and organizational growth objectives.
Assist with maintaining CompTech's professional website, marketing initiatives, and social media presence as appropriate.

Quality & Compliance

Ensure compliance with CompTech's Quality Management System (QMS) across assigned programs.
Lead continuous process improvement initiatives that improve quality, efficiency, and customer satisfaction.
Support the maintenance and continuous improvement of organizational certifications including:
ISO 9001
ISO 20000
ISO 27001
CMMI

Ensure compliance with Federal, state, local, contractual, and industry regulations and standards.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, Information Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
Minimum five (5) years of progressively responsible experience managing Federal Government programs, contracts, or large technical projects.
Demonstrated experience managing cross-functional teams supporting Government customers.
Working knowledge of Federal Government contracting, FAR, contract administration, and program lifecycle management.
Experience managing budgets, schedules, staffing, risk, and customer relationships.
Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and decision-making skills.
Knowledge of AI/ML, digital transformation, systems modernization, cloud technologies, and process automation.
Experience leading digital transformation, AI/ML, systems modernization, or enterprise IT initiatives.
Experience developing proposal strategies and writing Federal Government proposals is highly preferred.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Microsoft Teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Project Management Professional (PMP), Program Management Professional (PgMP), CAPM, or equivalent certification.
Experience supporting Department of Defense (DoD), Defense Logistics Agency (DLA), or other Federal civilian agencies.
Experience managing multi-disciplinary technical teams supporting IT, engineering, or professional services contracts.
Familiarity with proposal management and capture support activities.
Active Security Clearance or the ability to obtain one.

Federal Government Contract Administration
Customer Relationship Management
Financial & Schedule Management
Risk & Issue Management
Team Leadership & Staff Development
Business Operations
Proposal & Capture Support
Quality Management Systems
Strategic Planning
Continuous Process Improvement

Ability to occasionally lift up to 15 pounds.
Ability to travel up to 25% in support of customer meetings, contract transitions, program reviews, and corporate initiatives.

jobs.title: Senior Strategic Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Kestra Financial is a wealth management platform dedicated to empowering independent financial professionals—including traditional and hybrid RIAs—to grow their businesses and deliver exceptional client service. We combine advanced business management technology with personalized consulting to provide unmatched scale, efficiency, and support. Our advisor-focused culture is built on innovation and advocacy, enabling advisors to offer comprehensive securities and investment advisory solutions to their clients

Lead with Purpose. Partner with Impact

Kestra Financial, a leading provider of wealth management platforms, technology solutions, and investment products empowering independent financial advisors and RIAs nationwide, is seeking a Senior Strategic Implementation Manager.

This role serves as a pivotal execution leader accountable for the disciplined delivery of Kestra Wealth Management’s highest-priority strategic initiatives in investment products and platform capabilities. You will drive the successful launch of new investment products and manage end-to-end launch campaigns while coordinating complex cross-functional projects spanning technology, compliance, business development, and operations.

By implementing and championing agile, Scrum-like cadences and robust portfolio governance practices, you will build transparency, predictability, and accountability across initiatives. Your leadership will ensure that strategic intent translates into measurable business outcomes—including accelerated advisor adoption, revenue contribution from new products, enhanced platform capabilities, and operational excellence.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for a collaborative leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, execution, and cross-functional influence in a dynamic, growth-oriented wealth management environment.

What You’ll Do:

Own the end-to-end governance and planning that results in successful delivery of priority investment product launches (e.g., alternative investment solutions, insurance products, or curated offerings) and strategic platform implementation initiatives (new advisory revenue vertical, investment program redesign, etc) from concept through post-launch optimization and benefits realization.
Lead the coordination and execution of comprehensive launch campaigns, aligning go-to-market activities including sales enablement, marketing communications, advisor training and onboarding programs, distribution strategy, and adoption tracking to drive rapid uptake and sustained engagement.
Establish and maintain a prioritized portfolio of strategic initiatives for Investment Platforms & Products; drive rigorous sequencing, capacity alignment, funding discipline, and proactive trade-off decisions (scope, timeline, resources, investment) aligned to Kestra’s business objectives and growth priorities.
Partner with Product Management to translate product strategy and roadmap into executable implementation plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and success criteria.
Support Wealth Management platform and product leads by facilitating high-performing cross-functional project teams and workstreams involving:
Technology: Platform development, data integrations (including MDM/medallion architectures), APIs, advisor portals/tools, and infrastructure enhancements.
Compliance & Legal: Product due diligence, regulatory reviews/approvals, disclosures, risk assessments, and ongoing product governance to ensure adherence to SEC, FINRA, fiduciary, and other requirements.
Business: Commercialization strategy, RIA/advisor engagement and feedback loops, distribution channel readiness, pricing/packaging, and P&L impact modeling.
Operations & Finance: Operational readiness, process design, financial tracking, and benefits measurement.
Map and manage complex dependencies, risks, and interdependencies across teams; proactively identify and remove blockers while fostering alignment and shared ownership in a matrixed environment.
Ensure every initiative incorporates appropriate compliance guardrails, risk controls, audit readiness, and change management from the start.
Design, implement, and continuously mature agile delivery operating models tailored to regulated investment product and platform initiatives. This includes establishing Scrum-like cadences (sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives), Kanban for workflow transparency and flow optimization, and scaled frameworks (e.g., program-level planning or release management) for larger or interdependent efforts.
Stand up consistent governance rhythms and forums, including steering committees, launch readiness reviews/tollgates, dependency management sessions, risk reviews, and clear escalation paths to executive leadership.
Drive adoption of modern agile/project tools (Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or equivalent) and best practices to improve delivery velocity, predictability, collaboration, and quality across technology and business teams.
Champion a shift toward iterative, outcome-focused delivery—balancing the need for structure and compliance in product launches with the speed and adaptability required in a competitive wealth tech landscape.
Build and operate a portfolio “control tower” capability: deliver timely, credible, decision-oriented reporting and dashboards on initiative status, milestones, risks/issues, dependencies, financial performance (budget vs. plan, ROI tracking), and leading indicators of business impact.
Define, track, and report on key business outcome metrics tied to each strategic initiative (e.g., new product net flows/AUM/revenue contribution, advisor adoption and usage rates, client/advisor satisfaction or NPS impact, reduction in time-to-market or launch cycle time, compliance adherence, platform feature utilization and engagement).
Proactively surface execution risks, capacity constraints, and recommended trade-offs to senior leadership; lead structured issue resolution, corrective action planning, and recovery efforts to protect delivery commitments and protect/enhance business results.
Prepare and present high-quality materials for executive leadership, steering committees, and governance forums; represent the delivery health and outlook of the Investment Platforms & Products portfolio with clarity and fact-based insights.
Instill a culture of genuine accountability—where teams own and are measured on the delivery of agreed business outcomes and value realization, not merely activity completion or milestone hitting.

What You Bring: 

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or Software Engineering.
2+ years experience in technical product management in an Agile environment.
5+ years of experience in wealth management, investment operations, or trading
3-5+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic program/portfolio management, product implementation, launch execution, or enterprise transformation roles within wealth management, RIA platforms, investment product development, fintech, asset/wealth platforms, or similarly complex, regulated financial services environments.
Demonstrated success leading multiple end-to-end launches of investment products or major platform capabilities, including coordination across technology builds, compliance/regulatory approvals, and go-to-market execution
Direct experience with alternatives/private markets access, model portfolios, structured solutions, or advisor-facing technology platforms within a broker dealer organization is strongly preferred.
Track record of successfully implementing or significantly maturing agile delivery practices (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, hybrid, or tailored approaches) in product development or regulated contexts, with quantifiable improvements in predictability, velocity, and time-to-value.

Certifications and Licenses:

Series 7 , 63 or 66 required within 2 years.
Series 65 preferred

Internal applicants must be in good standing and have a minimum of 1 year of service with Kestra. Internal applicants must also have a minimum of 1 year service in current role unless approved by EVP.

Benefits to support you:

Competitive pay and benefits with a large employer (over 1600 employees nationwide)
401(k), health insurance, and a competitive benefits package
Work in a supportive, collaborative environment committed to professional excellence
Help clients navigate meaningful financial decisions with confidence
Opportunities for training, development, and long-term growth within the firm
Tuition reimbursement for qualified expenses

Our Mission is Powering Financial Independence, enabling the growth and success of investing clients and the advisors who serve them. We do that by living our values: Serve, Make it Happen, and One team.
