Kestra Financial is a wealth management platform dedicated to empowering independent financial professionals—including traditional and hybrid RIAs—to grow their businesses and deliver exceptional client service. We combine advanced business management technology with personalized consulting to provide unmatched scale, efficiency, and support. Our advisor-focused culture is built on innovation and advocacy, enabling advisors to offer comprehensive securities and investment advisory solutions to their clients

Lead with Purpose. Partner with Impact

Kestra Financial, a leading provider of wealth management platforms, technology solutions, and investment products empowering independent financial advisors and RIAs nationwide, is seeking a Senior Strategic Implementation Manager.

This role serves as a pivotal execution leader accountable for the disciplined delivery of Kestra Wealth Management’s highest-priority strategic initiatives in investment products and platform capabilities. You will drive the successful launch of new investment products and manage end-to-end launch campaigns while coordinating complex cross-functional projects spanning technology, compliance, business development, and operations.

By implementing and championing agile, Scrum-like cadences and robust portfolio governance practices, you will build transparency, predictability, and accountability across initiatives. Your leadership will ensure that strategic intent translates into measurable business outcomes—including accelerated advisor adoption, revenue contribution from new products, enhanced platform capabilities, and operational excellence.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for a collaborative leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, execution, and cross-functional influence in a dynamic, growth-oriented wealth management environment.

What You’ll Do:

Own the end-to-end governance and planning that results in successful delivery of priority investment product launches (e.g., alternative investment solutions, insurance products, or curated offerings) and strategic platform implementation initiatives (new advisory revenue vertical, investment program redesign, etc) from concept through post-launch optimization and benefits realization.
Lead the coordination and execution of comprehensive launch campaigns, aligning go-to-market activities including sales enablement, marketing communications, advisor training and onboarding programs, distribution strategy, and adoption tracking to drive rapid uptake and sustained engagement.
Establish and maintain a prioritized portfolio of strategic initiatives for Investment Platforms & Products; drive rigorous sequencing, capacity alignment, funding discipline, and proactive trade-off decisions (scope, timeline, resources, investment) aligned to Kestra’s business objectives and growth priorities.
Partner with Product Management to translate product strategy and roadmap into executable implementation plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and success criteria.
Support Wealth Management platform and product leads by facilitating high-performing cross-functional project teams and workstreams involving:
Technology: Platform development, data integrations (including MDM/medallion architectures), APIs, advisor portals/tools, and infrastructure enhancements.
Compliance & Legal: Product due diligence, regulatory reviews/approvals, disclosures, risk assessments, and ongoing product governance to ensure adherence to SEC, FINRA, fiduciary, and other requirements.
Business: Commercialization strategy, RIA/advisor engagement and feedback loops, distribution channel readiness, pricing/packaging, and P&L impact modeling.
Operations & Finance: Operational readiness, process design, financial tracking, and benefits measurement.
Map and manage complex dependencies, risks, and interdependencies across teams; proactively identify and remove blockers while fostering alignment and shared ownership in a matrixed environment.
Ensure every initiative incorporates appropriate compliance guardrails, risk controls, audit readiness, and change management from the start.
Design, implement, and continuously mature agile delivery operating models tailored to regulated investment product and platform initiatives. This includes establishing Scrum-like cadences (sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives), Kanban for workflow transparency and flow optimization, and scaled frameworks (e.g., program-level planning or release management) for larger or interdependent efforts.
Stand up consistent governance rhythms and forums, including steering committees, launch readiness reviews/tollgates, dependency management sessions, risk reviews, and clear escalation paths to executive leadership.
Drive adoption of modern agile/project tools (Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or equivalent) and best practices to improve delivery velocity, predictability, collaboration, and quality across technology and business teams.
Champion a shift toward iterative, outcome-focused delivery—balancing the need for structure and compliance in product launches with the speed and adaptability required in a competitive wealth tech landscape.
Build and operate a portfolio “control tower” capability: deliver timely, credible, decision-oriented reporting and dashboards on initiative status, milestones, risks/issues, dependencies, financial performance (budget vs. plan, ROI tracking), and leading indicators of business impact.
Define, track, and report on key business outcome metrics tied to each strategic initiative (e.g., new product net flows/AUM/revenue contribution, advisor adoption and usage rates, client/advisor satisfaction or NPS impact, reduction in time-to-market or launch cycle time, compliance adherence, platform feature utilization and engagement).
Proactively surface execution risks, capacity constraints, and recommended trade-offs to senior leadership; lead structured issue resolution, corrective action planning, and recovery efforts to protect delivery commitments and protect/enhance business results.
Prepare and present high-quality materials for executive leadership, steering committees, and governance forums; represent the delivery health and outlook of the Investment Platforms & Products portfolio with clarity and fact-based insights.
Instill a culture of genuine accountability—where teams own and are measured on the delivery of agreed business outcomes and value realization, not merely activity completion or milestone hitting.

What You Bring: 

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or Software Engineering.
2+ years experience in technical product management in an Agile environment.
5+ years of experience in wealth management, investment operations, or trading
3-5+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic program/portfolio management, product implementation, launch execution, or enterprise transformation roles within wealth management, RIA platforms, investment product development, fintech, asset/wealth platforms, or similarly complex, regulated financial services environments.
Demonstrated success leading multiple end-to-end launches of investment products or major platform capabilities, including coordination across technology builds, compliance/regulatory approvals, and go-to-market execution
Direct experience with alternatives/private markets access, model portfolios, structured solutions, or advisor-facing technology platforms within a broker dealer organization is strongly preferred.
Track record of successfully implementing or significantly maturing agile delivery practices (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, hybrid, or tailored approaches) in product development or regulated contexts, with quantifiable improvements in predictability, velocity, and time-to-value.

Certifications and Licenses:

Series 65 preferred

Internal Application Policy:

Internal applicants must be in good standing and have a minimum of 1 year of service with Kestra. Internal applicants must also have a minimum of 1 year service in current role unless approved by EVP.

Benefits to support you:

Competitive pay and benefits with a large employer (over 1600 employees nationwide)
401(k), health insurance, and a competitive benefits package
Work in a supportive, collaborative environment committed to professional excellence
Help clients navigate meaningful financial decisions with confidence
Opportunities for training, development, and long-term growth within the firm
Tuition reimbursement for qualified expenses

Kestra Values:

Our Mission is Powering Financial Independence, enabling the growth and success of investing clients and the advisors who serve them. We do that by living our values: Serve, Make it Happen, and One team.

Provide senior military operations analysis and subject matter expertise in one or more warfare areas or domains. Analyze U.S. and adversary concepts of operations, tactics, techniques, and procedures to inform system development, capability assessment, and operational employment.
Serve as a technical and operational advisor to program managers, development teams, and DoD stakeholders for the evaluation, transition, and fielding of advanced warfighting tools and technologies.
Assess how emerging systems and software capabilities support military operations, command and control processes, fires execution, and current or future Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures.
Provide on-site operational and technical support during daily operations, exercises, demonstrations, integration events, and field experimentation.
Train operators and military staff on advanced warfighting software, hardware, and supporting systems to ensure mission readiness and effective operational employment.
Serve as the primary field interface between warfighters, technical program managers, software developers, and system engineers.
Support system configuration, operator workflow development, and user adoption during technology transition and fielding efforts.
Provide real-time troubleshooting during operational use, exercises, demonstrations, and experimentation events.
Coordinate with technical experts, software developers, and system engineers to resolve hardware, software, network, and configuration issues.
Support routine maintenance, emergency troubleshooting, and sustainment activities to ensure systems remain mission-ready.
Evaluate system performance and operational effectiveness in support of military staff processes and current TTPs.
Identify operational gaps, technical limitations, workflow issues, and opportunities to improve system employment in high-stakes operational environments.

Serve as a forward-deployed liaison officer (LNO) to designated Combatant Command or field sites, acting as the program’s on-site representative for operational coordination, user engagement, and system integration.
Facilitate communication between program leadership, warfighters, and technical teams to ensure operational requirements, system issues, and emerging needs are accurately captured and rapidly addressed.
Support planning, execution, and assessment of operational events, readiness activities, experimentation, and technology transition efforts occurring at assigned commands or sites.
Provide day-to-day guidance, troubleshooting, training, and workflow support to operators employing advanced warfighting tools and technologies in real-world or exercise environments.

5+ years of experience working in a multi-level security environment.
Experience leading and managing teams to solve complex technical, management, and administrative challenges.
Demonstrated ability to conduct research and analysis using incomplete information, develop clear analytic products, and present results effectively.
Excellent interpersonal communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel).
Strong documentation, writing, and reporting skills.
Must be a self-starter with the ability to take initiative, work independently, and elevate issues appropriately.

Master's Degree preferred

TS/SCI

The role reports directly to the Corporate Director of Investigations and Insider Threat and serves as a principal advisor to the Aeronautics Sector Senior Security Director, as well as other sector and company leadership. This position is located in M
elbourne, FL OR Palmdale, CA,
and due to the dynamic environment and size of both the sector and the company, domestic and international travel is required.

Primary Responsibilities

Sector & Enterprise Leadership

Provide sector-wide leadership for investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence activities, set priorities and ensure effective allocation of investigative and analytic resources.
Serve as an enterprise leader and thought partner by helping to shape and implement policies, procedures, workflows, initiatives, and cross-sector teaming efforts.
Develop and maintain procedures, operating standards, and investigative protocols.
Track program performance using key metrics and preparing reports, dashboards, and executive summaries.
Recommend improvements which enhance operational effectiveness, regulatory compliance, and customer service.
Maintain well-established liaison relationships in the investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence arenas with law enforcement, prosecutorial agencies, and the intelligence community, such as DCSA, FBI, AFOSI, and NCIS.

Enterprise Investigations

Manage the corporate investigations program for the sector, including allegations of insider threat activity, counterintelligence concerns, workplace violence, fraud, misconduct, theft, policy violations, and other security-related incidents.
Lead and oversee investigators and case work to ensure fair, objective, legally defensible investigations and compliance with government, customer, and corporate policies, procedures, and practices.
Conduct and oversee insider threat and counterintelligence investigations consistent with applicable government and corporate protocols.
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders for investigations and operations.
Review investigative findings, ensure appropriate documentation and evidence preservation, and recommend corrective and preventive actions.
Monitor metrics and trends to identify systemic risks, emerging issues, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Insider Threat & Risk Management

Lead and administer the sector’s Insider Threat Program, while helping to shape and inform the company’s overall insider threat program through data, gap and trend analysis, and operational insights.
Monitor and analyze security incidents and investigative trends to identify emerging risks, including insider threats.
Develop and implement strategies to address potential threats, risks, and vulnerabilities.

Security & Compliance

Oversee investigations of security complaints and compliance concerns while ensuring consistent application of company policies, procedures, and standards.
Interpret, apply, and ensure adherence to federal security regulations that govern company operations, including the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), DOD Manual 5205.07 Special Access Program Security Manual, Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), and other applicable directives.
Monitor regulatory changes and assist with updates to policies, procedures, and compliance programs.

Training & Awareness

Develop and deliver security education and awareness, and implement corporate investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence programs across cleared and uncleared facilities.

Stakeholder & Agency Partnerships

Build collaborative relationships across the sector and company to ensure aligned decision-making and consistent execution.
Partner closely with Ethics, Labor and Employment, Employee Relations, Cybersecurity, Human Resources, Legal, Compliance, security counterparts, business leaders, and relevant government agencies (e.g., DCSA) to identify and mitigate company risks and insider threats, strengthen compliance, and protect company assets.
Coordinate information sharing between internal stakeholders and external law enforcement and government entities to support security investigations and broader security objectives, partnering with Legal as appropriate.
Support government reporting requirements and regulatory inquiries, in coordination with internal stakeholders and government partners.

People Leadership

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team responsible for investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence.
Lead, mentor, and develop team members fostering a culture of integrity, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Model and promote a self‑starter culture grounded in uncompromising integrity and ethical behavior in all activities.
Establish team priorities, assign work, and monitor workload, quality, and performance.
Support workforce planning, hiring, onboarding, performance management, and employee development.
Represent the team effectively with senior leadership and other stakeholders through clear briefings, written reports, and executive-ready communications.
Demonstrate strong interpersonal skills and a highly collaborative, team-oriented leadership style, with the ability to build trust, influence without authority, and work effectively across diverse stakeholder groups.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and 10 years of relevant experience outlined below OR Master’s degree and 8 years of relevant experience outlined below.
Candidates must have a current U.S. Government Top Secret level security clearance, and must have the ability to obtain, and maintain both SCI and Special Access Program access. Candidates must be willing to undergo polygraph and extensive background checks for clearance and access eligibility.
Must have at least 8 years experience in one or more of the following areas: law enforcement, insider threat, counterintelligence, security, compliance, or risk management.
Must have at least 8 years of experience leading and managing investigations in support of national security or national industrial security programs, including regulatory and/or security compliance matters.
Must have at least 8 years of people leadership and/or program management experience.
Demonstrated high level of integrity, sound judgment, and discretion in handling sensitive and confidential matters.
Strong knowledge of investigative methodologies, insider threat, counterintelligence, and risk management principles.
Significant experience conducting workplace investigations and subject/witness/victim interviews, with a proven ability to read behavioral indicators, build rapport, and elicit relevant information.
Excellent communication, leadership, analytical, and decision-making skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred advanced degree (e.g., Master’s in Criminal Justice, Intelligence, Strategic Intelligence, Homeland Security, Security Studies, Business, Law, or a related field).

Job Summary

The Manager, Information Security is responsible for strengthening and maintaining an organization's overall information security posture. This role provides leadership across security governance, risk and compliance, and security operations while partnering with IT teams and business leadership to identify and mitigate security risks. The position will oversee security technologies, operational processes, compliance initiatives, and technical security personnel to ensure the organization maintains effective protections across its network, systems, identities, applications, and cloud environments.

Develop, maintain, and improve information security policies, procedures, standards, and governance processes.
Lead security risk management activities, including threat intelligence, risk assessments, risk analysis, and mitigation planning.
Manage security compliance programs, including ISO 27001, ISO 27701, PCI-DSS, client assessments, audits, and security questionnaires.
Oversee security resources, budgets, vendors, and managed security service providers.
Lead security awareness and training initiatives and advise IT, leadership, and business teams regarding emerging threats, policies, controls, and security best practices.
Review security architecture and designs for network, systems, applications, identity, collaboration, and cloud infrastructure.
Manage ongoing security monitoring, testing, audits, remediation activities, and compliance tracking.
Oversee security detection and response capabilities, including log aggregation, correlation, analysis, incident response, and recovery.
Provide leadership and oversight for security technologies and operational functions, including firewalls, network segmentation, vulnerability management, privileged and remote access, EDR/NGAV, SIEM, email security, and continuous monitoring.
Lead and prioritize security projects, administrative initiatives, and continuous improvement efforts.
Manage, mentor, and develop technical security engineering personnel.
Collaborate with IT, business leadership, and other stakeholders to identify security requirements and implement appropriate controls.

jobs.description:
Important Application Submission Information

In order to ensure your application is successfully received before the job posting expires, please submit your application by 11:59 PM on Wednesday, September 2, 2026

More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

The preferred location is Plainfield, Noblesville, or Huntington. The manager will consider locations in the Northern Indiana Region. The exact location will be determined at the time of offer based on business needs.

This position manages, inspects, and protects a designated portion of the approximate 33,000 miles of purchased easement and fee owned Transmission corridors to ensure customers, contractors, and developers are in compliance with the established AP guidelines. The position collaborates with and presents guidelines to stakeholders and customers and participates in the decision making of the release of transmission easements and selling of fee owned property. In performing the duties, this position must review technical engineering drawings and site plans to ensure that customers, contractors, and developers comply with Duke Energy's guidelines and recorded property rights documents. Engineering plan reviews require a general knowledge of engineering standards, construction standards and techniques, future transmission planning, OSHA rules, NESC rules, as well as other applicable rules. Duties also include the removal of existing encroachments and execution of relevant encroachment agreements. The job requires legal involvement in which the position must be able to maintain detailed documentation, read and interpret legal documents, give depositions, and testify in a court of law.

Depending upon the desired qualifications of the successful applicant, the hiring manager may elect to fill this position at a higher level within the job hierarchy

Responsibilities:

Resolves existing encroachments & Helicopter Reports of encroachments.
This involves negotiating with customers, reviewing, and effectively communicating to customers Duke’s legal rights while pursuing an appropriate course of action.
In some cases, will involve court action and testifying and will require an empathic approach.
Collaborate with observer during Helicopter flight.
Reviews and approves technical engineering drawings (site plans, grading, utilities, landscaping, etc.) to ensure compliance to Duke Energy’s transmission guidelines.
This includes evaluating grade changes to protect and ensure the National Electric Safety Code issues, OSHA minimum approach distances, and Duke Energy minimum clearance standards are not violated.
Meets with developers, architects, engineers, corporate executives, governmental leaders, and lawyers to prevent and resolve encroachment issues created during the plan reviews above.
Prepares professional letters to property owners outlining plan review findings.
Document – detailed conversations, site visits, emails, etc., to support potential review by management or legal team for court action.
With Management oversight, this involves negotiating with customers, reviewing, and effectively communicating Duke’s legal rights to customers while pursuing and recommending an appropriate course of action.
In some cases, this will involve court action and testifying.
Meets with developers, architects, engineers, corporate executives, governmental leaders, and lawyers to resolve encroachment issues that are not resolved at the employee level.
Train, onboard and mentor new employees
Responds to customers and community concerns associated with our AP Programs
Identifies and assigns opportunities for Asset Protection team members to meet with influential leaders to develop a relationship that enhances our ability to prevent encroachments.
Evaluates, recommends, and attends conferences of Professional Land Surveyors, Home Builders, Professional Engineers and Grading Contractors Associations, etc. that are most effective for Asset Protection to attend each year.
Works with government agencies, including DOT and Environmental to ensure compliance with appropriate state and federal regulations and proactive communications of area vegetation management plans and procedures to community stakeholders.
This includes meeting with City/County Planning Boards, Architectural & Engineering Firms, major developers of commercial and residential developments and others who have the ability to encroach on transmission easements.
Assists with activities for escalated projects across the enterprise.
Monitor the performance of contract resources to assure safe work practices, asset protection procedures/standards adherence, and productivity consistent with Duke Energy Expectations
Assist the Lead AP Program Manager as needed for effective coordination and participation during emergency storm operations.
Works with minimal supervision on complex issues
Applying advanced knowledge and problem-solving skills to wide-ranging issues
Integrates industry knowledge related to data into everyday business practices and decision making.
Manages expenditures within region and area of responsibility to ensure that budget target and forecast changes are met.
Implement adjustments within region and area of responsibility to complete necessary work while meeting budget forecasts, including forecast changes.
Participates in and may be required to testify in court issues (meetings with property owner council, depositions, and trial)
Provide and assist in the collection of legal documentation in preparation for any Asset Protection legal action to give depositions or testify in court concerning unresolved encroachment issues.
Coordinates the accumulation of supporting evidence, documenting the case from the beginning to support legal action.

Note: This posting is for one position. Dependent on relevant experience, the level to which a candidate is aligned is outlined below.

Asset Protection Program Manager

Basic/Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in communications, Forestry, Engineering, Real Estate, Business other related discipline
In lieu of associate degree High School Diploma/GED and seven (7) years minimum related work experience.
Valid Driver's License

Valid Driver's License

Additional Preferred Qualifications

Possess working knowledge of how AP affects the safety and reliability of the electrical system.
Project management work experience and/or PMI© Knowledge
Familiarity with GIS databases, mapping and othe geo-spatial systems
Utility Experience – Working knowledge to proficiency
Demonstrated organizational, planning and time management skills
Demonstrated effective communication and customer relation skills, both verbal and written, including strong presentation skills
Demonstrated collaboration skills and teamwork

Demonstrated ability to deal with highly stressful situations
Demonstrated ability to collaborate with multiple levels within an organization
Demonstrated ability to get work done through use of contractors.

Demonstrated ability to work independently and is a self motivator, self initiator, and is able to make decisions and supervise/self manage
Demonstrated ability to read engineering plans
Demonstrated ability to read easement documents

Demonstrated familiarity with NESC & OSHA requirements for the electric business
Demonstrated attention to detail

As a key member of the centralized NG Investigations, Insider Threat, and Counterintelligence Team, this role has primary responsibility for that sector while also enabling and supporting aligned investigative and insider threat efforts across the company. The role reports directly to the Corporate Director of Investigations and Insider Threat and serves as a principal advisor to the Aeronautics Sector Senior Security Director, as well as other sector and company leadership. This position is located in M
elbourne, FL OR Palmdale, CA,
and due to the dynamic environment and size of both the sector and the company, domestic and international travel is required.

Primary Responsibilities

Sector & Enterprise Leadership

Provide sector-wide leadership for investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence activities, set priorities and ensure effective allocation of investigative and analytic resources.
Serve as an enterprise leader and thought partner by helping to shape and implement policies, procedures, workflows, initiatives, and cross-sector teaming efforts.
Develop and maintain procedures, operating standards, and investigative protocols.
Track program performance using key metrics and preparing reports, dashboards, and executive summaries.
Recommend improvements which enhance operational effectiveness, regulatory compliance, and customer service.
Maintain well-established liaison relationships in the investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence arenas with law enforcement, prosecutorial agencies, and the intelligence community, such as DCSA, FBI, AFOSI, and NCIS.

Enterprise Investigations

Manage the corporate investigations program for the sector, including allegations of insider threat activity, counterintelligence concerns, workplace violence, fraud, misconduct, theft, policy violations, and other security-related incidents.
Lead and oversee investigators and case work to ensure fair, objective, legally defensible investigations and compliance with government, customer, and corporate policies, procedures, and practices.
Conduct and oversee insider threat and counterintelligence investigations consistent with applicable government and corporate protocols.
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders for investigations and operations.
Review investigative findings, ensure appropriate documentation and evidence preservation, and recommend corrective and preventive actions.
Monitor metrics and trends to identify systemic risks, emerging issues, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Insider Threat & Risk Management

Lead and administer the sector’s Insider Threat Program, while helping to shape and inform the company’s overall insider threat program through data, gap and trend analysis, and operational insights.
Monitor and analyze security incidents and investigative trends to identify emerging risks, including insider threats.
Develop and implement strategies to address potential threats, risks, and vulnerabilities.

Security & Compliance

Oversee investigations of security complaints and compliance concerns while ensuring consistent application of company policies, procedures, and standards.
Interpret, apply, and ensure adherence to federal security regulations that govern company operations, including the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), DOD Manual 5205.07 Special Access Program Security Manual, Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), and other applicable directives.
Monitor regulatory changes and assist with updates to policies, procedures, and compliance programs.

Training & Awareness

Develop and deliver security education and awareness, and implement corporate investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence programs across cleared and uncleared facilities.

Stakeholder & Agency Partnerships

Build collaborative relationships across the sector and company to ensure aligned decision-making and consistent execution.
Partner closely with Ethics, Labor and Employment, Employee Relations, Cybersecurity, Human Resources, Legal, Compliance, security counterparts, business leaders, and relevant government agencies (e.g., DCSA) to identify and mitigate company risks and insider threats, strengthen compliance, and protect company assets.
Coordinate information sharing between internal stakeholders and external law enforcement and government entities to support security investigations and broader security objectives, partnering with Legal as appropriate.
Support government reporting requirements and regulatory inquiries, in coordination with internal stakeholders and government partners.

People Leadership

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team responsible for investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence.
Lead, mentor, and develop team members fostering a culture of integrity, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Model and promote a self‑starter culture grounded in uncompromising integrity and ethical behavior in all activities.
Establish team priorities, assign work, and monitor workload, quality, and performance.
Support workforce planning, hiring, onboarding, performance management, and employee development.
Represent the team effectively with senior leadership and other stakeholders through clear briefings, written reports, and executive-ready communications.
Demonstrate strong interpersonal skills and a highly collaborative, team-oriented leadership style, with the ability to build trust, influence without authority, and work effectively across diverse stakeholder groups.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and 10 years of relevant experience outlined below OR Master’s degree and 8 years of relevant experience outlined below.
Candidates must have a current U.S. Government Top Secret level security clearance, and must have the ability to obtain, and maintain both SCI and Special Access Program access. Candidates must be willing to undergo polygraph and extensive background checks for clearance and access eligibility.
Must have at least 8 years experience in one or more of the following areas: law enforcement, insider threat, counterintelligence, security, compliance, or risk management.
Must have at least 8 years of experience leading and managing investigations in support of national security or national industrial security programs, including regulatory and/or security compliance matters.
Must have at least 8 years of people leadership and/or program management experience.
Demonstrated high level of integrity, sound judgment, and discretion in handling sensitive and confidential matters.
Strong knowledge of investigative methodologies, insider threat, counterintelligence, and risk management principles.
Significant experience conducting workplace investigations and subject/witness/victim interviews, with a proven ability to read behavioral indicators, build rapport, and elicit relevant information.
Excellent communication, leadership, analytical, and decision-making skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred advanced degree (e.g., Master’s in Criminal Justice, Intelligence, Strategic Intelligence, Homeland Security, Security Studies, Business, Law, or a related field).
Preferred equivalencies include successful completion of one or more of the following, with a certificate or transcript provided upon application:
Federal Law Enforcement Training Center’s (FLETC) Criminal Investigator Training Program (CITP), or
An equivalent federal training program (e.g., FBI, DEA, or U.S. Postal Inspection Service).

Program management experience, including budgeting, reporting, and strategic planning.
Demonstrated understanding of security requirements supporting dynamic business units that execute high-value contracts across a broad US Government customer base.
Knowledge of processes related to program security, industrial security requirements, supply chain security, workplace violence prevention, security awareness, asset protection, and ITAR/export related security measures.
Experience with NISPOM, FAR, and other federal security regulations, including interpreting, applying, and ensuring adherence to these requirements in the context of security investigations, insider threat, and counterintelligence.

The PKI Deputy Contract Program Manager will serve as the secondary representative for the Air Force Public Key Infrastructure (AF PKI) Program contract, overseeing all mission support work and ensuring adherence to specified standards. The Deputy Contract Program Manager will help manage functional, capability, and delivery teams within a structured framework, requiring a seasoned leader with expertise in project management, PKI operations, and contract oversight within a Department of the Air Force (DAF) context.

Job Duties

Project Oversight: Act as the secondary representative responsible for overseeing all direct mission support work under the contract, ensuring compliance with all referenced standards and requirements.

Quality and Configuration Control: Maintain quality assurance and configuration control for all products and services provided to and by the AF PKI program, ensuring consistency and reliability.

Management Approach: Implement a systematic management process to support PWS processes and requirements, coordinating functional, integrated capability, and product delivery teams within a controlled structure.

Schedule Development: Provide detailed program/project schedules for tasks and activities outlined in the PWS, ensuring compatibility with Microsoft Project for export and review. Develop a single Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) that will include all activities to sustain the AF PKI, activities supporting DoD PKI implementation, evolution of AF PKI capabilities, and other activities.

Financial Reviews: Meet monthly with the Government PM to review contract funding status, including labor forecast versus actual, cumulative travel costs, and cumulative Other Direct Costs (ODCs), to ensure fiscal accountability.

Continuity of Operations (COOP): Collaborate with the Government to identify AF PKI SPO essential functions and operations requiring uninterrupted availability. Develop, maintain, and test a comprehensive COOP. Deliver the initial COOP to the Government on an agreed date, no later than six months after the contract start date of June 1, 2025.

External Meeting Participation: Ensure team representation in DoD and AF recurring meetings regarding PKI (ex. Summits, Program Information Exchanges, working groups). Ensure preparedness and professional conduct of AF PKI contractor representatives in meetings.

Required Qualifications

Project Management: Proven experience leading complex technical projects, preferably in cybersecurity or PKI programs, with oversight of multiple teams and deliverables.

PKI Knowledge: Familiarity with PKI systems and operations within a DoD or DAF environment, ensuring alignment with program goals.

Quality Assurance: Expertise in maintaining quality assurance and configuration control for technical products and services.

Scheduling Skills: Proficiency in developing and managing project schedules, with experience using Microsoft Project or similar tools.

Financial Oversight: Ability to track and review contract funding, including labor, travel, and ODCs, with strong analytical and reporting skills.

Leadership: Strong ability to coordinate and manage diverse teams within a structured framework, ensuring systematic execution of tasks.

Security Clearance: Must possess or be eligible to obtain and maintain a minimum Secret clearance, with all employees cleared to at least Secret by the contract start date of June 1, 2025.

Location: Ability to work in San Antonio, TX, with potential on-site support at the Government-leased facility for oversight and coordination.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in related field.

Preferred Qualifications

Security Clearance: Active Top Secret (TS) or Top Secret /Secure Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance.

DAF PKI Experience: Prior leadership role in an AF PKI or similar DoD program, providing context for program-specific standards and processes.

Certifications: Relevant certifications such as Project Management Professional (PMP), CompTIA Security+, or DoD 8570/8140-approved Information Assurance certifications (e.g., IAT Level II or higher).

Team Management: Extensive experience managing functional, capability, and delivery teams in a controlled, systematic environment.

Financial Acumen: Background in contract financial management, with a track record of accurate forecasting and cost control.

Communication: Exceptional skills in presenting schedules and financial updates to Government stakeholders, ensuring clarity and alignment.

Lead and deliver complex programs with cross-organizational impact, operating across multiple organizations within Prime Video
Drive clarity in ambiguous spaces where the problem, strategy, and solution path may not yet be fully defined

Description

Do you want to shape how Amazon builds its next generation of consumer devices — not by building one product, but by building the system that makes all products better? As the Program Management Office (PMO) Lead and steward of Amazon Devices Product Development Process (PDP) within the Hardware Strategy & Operations team, you will own the framework that every hardware program at Amazon Devices runs on. You will drive the evolution of how we develop devices — from the earliest customer-focused working backwards documents through production validation — ensuring that hundreds of engineers across disciplines and geographies have the clarity, tools, and process they need to deliver on time, at quality, and at scale.

Key job responsibilities

Own the end-to-end Product Development Process (PDP) for Amazon Devices Hardware, including phase definitions, gate criteria, milestone templates, approver matrices, and associated tools — ensuring the process remains current, scalable, and aligned with how programs actually execute.
Identify, scope, and lead strategic process improvement initiatives from proposal through implementation, partnering with cross-functional stakeholders across engineering, operations, finance, and product management to drive adoption and measure impact.
Maintain and evolve the suite of PDP tools and templates — including milestone documents (Product Assessment, Business Requirements Document, Development Commit, xVT Readiness Reviews, Announce Risk Review, OK2Ship), checklists, and the Milestone Manager — to reduce friction and enable program teams to move with speed and confidence.
Serve as the primary point of contact and subject matter expert for PDP across the Hardware organization, providing guidance to System TPMs and functional leads on process application, change management, and escalation paths.
Drive cross-functional alignment on process changes, communicating updates clearly to stakeholders at all levels and ensuring the PDP Confluence space reflects the current state of the process at all times.

A day in the life

You start your day reviewing feedback from System Technical Program Managers (TPMs) across multiple device programs about friction points in the milestone review process. In the afternoon, you are driving a process improvement initiative — evaluating how the phase-gate methodology can better accommodate programs that blend hardware and software development. You close the day by updating the PDP Wiki page with revised templates and publishing a summary of approved process changes to the broader Hardware organization.

No two days look the same. You operate across teams and functions — partnering with Product Managers, System TPMs, Engineering leads, Operations Program Managers, and executive stakeholders — to keep the process current, practical, and effective 7. You are equally comfortable writing a detailed process specification and presenting a strategic recommendation to senior leadership.

About The Team

The Hardware Strategy & Operations team sits at the center of Amazon Devices hardware development. Our mission is to enable the Hardware organization to build the right products, the right way, at the right time. We own the mechanisms, processes, and tools that the broader Hardware organization depends on to execute — from pre-concept through production and sustaining.

Our world depends on rocks, minerals, metals and other raw materials – the building blocks of modern society. As an industry leader, Metso helps transform these essential materials to enable sustainable modern life.

Our solutions and services support everything from renewable energy and electrification to the infrastructure and digital economy shaping our future. Together, we help our customers meet growing demand while driving the industry toward a more sustainable use of the earth’s natural resources.

Join nearly 18,000 Metsonites worldwide, each bringing unique expertise and experience to positive change. At Metso, you’re supported by a growth culture built on safety, wellbeing, inclusion and collaboration.

This is your opportunity to make an impact and rise above the possible.

Introduction

We are looking for a Project Manager
to join our Market Area North and Central America Project Delivery team
. In this role, you will be responsible for leading the execution of major customer contracts involving the design, retrofit, manufacturing, and installation of equipment and systems. You will ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with contractual commitments, contributing to customer success and profitable business growth.

You will report to the Project Delivery Manager.

This role is based in Canada, the United States, or Mexico, with flexible working options available. Relocation is not provided for this role.

This role includes approximately 20% travel to customer sites and project locations across North America and other international destinations.

Team you will belong to

You will join a team of experienced project delivery professionals focused on executing complex capital equipment and systems projects for customers in the mining and aggregates industries. Our team plays a key role in ensuring successful project execution, customer satisfaction, and the delivery of Metso's industry-leading solutions, with a shared focus on safety, quality, collaboration, and operational excellence.

We collaborate closely with customers, engineering teams, procurement specialists, manufacturing facilities, field service personnel, subcontractors, and business stakeholders. Our team is based across North and Central America, and our ways of working emphasize open and honest communication, customer focus, accountability, and getting things done together.

What You'll Do

Lead the execution of major customer contracts from project kickoff through final closeout.
Establish project plans, budgets, schedules, and cash flow forecasts while monitoring performance and initiating corrective actions when required.
Coordinate engineering, procurement, manufacturing, and field execution activities to ensure successful project delivery.
Review drawings, specifications, and requisitions to ensure compliance with contract requirements and project objectives.
Resolve technical, commercial, client, subcontractor, and cross-functional project issues.
Participate in the selection and management of subcontractors and major equipment suppliers.
Manage field activities, staffing requirements, and site coordination while promoting a strong safety culture.
Build trusted customer relationships, identify opportunities to address customer challenges, and support the delivery of value-added technical solutions.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or a related discipline, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum 5 years of project management experience in industrial, engineering, manufacturing, construction, or capital equipment environments.
Experience with engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction contracts, scheduling, quality management, and cost control.
Strong knowledge of contract administration, commercial terms, and project execution methodologies.
Excellent communication, stakeholder management, negotiation, and customer relationship skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced, international environment.
Mechanical and/or electrical aptitude with the ability to interpret technical drawings and specifications.
Fluency in French and/or Spanish, SAP Project Module experience, and knowledge of engineering or regulatory standards such as CSA or NEMA are considered assets.

What's In It For You

At Metso, you will combine meaningful work with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact in a supportive and inclusive environment. You'll be part of a global team where collaboration, wellbeing, and continuous learning are part of everyday work.

We support your growth and wellbeing by offering:

Purpose-led work: Contribute to enabling sustainable modern life and transforming the industry.

Rewards: Competitive compensation and performance-based incentives.
Flexibility: Hybrid working options to support balance and productivity.

Competitive benefits plan
Healthy living rewards
Mental wellbeing services
Annual leave starting at 15 days per calendar year
Engagement surveys
Global incentive program tied to business and performance targets

This is a client-side Project Manager opportunity with a global data centre developer delivering projects at a scale and complexity well beyond typical commercial builds. The role sits within a billion-dollar precinct and forms part of a long-term delivery program rather than a one-off project.

The position is predominantly site-based in Melbourne's western suburbs and reports directly to a Project Director. This is a delivery role, not an advisory or design-led position. The project is now at the fit-out stage and is heavy services-orientated. You will be working at the coalface of the project, supporting day-to-day delivery across program inputs, contractor and consultant coordination, sequencing, issue resolution and site-based decision-making for a highly technical fit-out.

This project requires people who have been embedded on complex live builds and understand how projects actually move on-site. Experience must come from environments such as data centres, hospitals, critical infrastructure, automation-led facilities, laboratories or similarly complex projects where service integration, commissioning and coordination are central to delivery. Candidates from architecture, design-only or advisory backgrounds without live construction delivery experience will not be suited.

The team works in a practical, delivery-led way and has built strong camaraderie on-site. The company has a genuinely good culture, with an approachable leadership team and people who work closely together to keep delivery moving. People are expected to take ownership, communicate clearly and stay close to the details. This is not a role for someone looking to manage from a distance or operate primarily from an office environment.

This role would suit a construction Senior Project Engineer, Senior Project Coordinator or a delivery-focused Project Manager who has worked on large, technically complex projects and is ready to step into a client-side role while remaining heavily involved in construction.

The role is site-based but flexible. There is scope to work from home one day per week, or from the inner-CBD head office one day per week, when appropriate. The expectation, however, is that the right person wants to be on-site and engaged with the project.

The salary for this role is up to a $240k package plus annual bonus, depending on experience.

Field Services Project Manager

About The Role

We are seeking a highly motivated Field Services Project Manager
to lead the successful execution of customer projects within our services organization. In this role, you will be responsible for managing the full project lifecycle, ensuring safe, profitable, and on-time delivery while maintaining exceptional customer satisfaction.

As the primary point of contact for customers throughout project execution, you will coordinate cross-functional teams, oversee project performance, manage risks, and drive operational excellence from project initiation through closeout.

What Will You Do?

Project Leadership & Execution

Manage the execution of field services projects in accordance with company policies, processes, and contractual requirements.
Lead cross-functional project teams, including engineering, planning, procurement, technical support, and field service resources.
Conduct project handovers and review project scope, deliverables, budgets, schedules, and risks.
Establish project governance, milestones, resource plans, and communication strategies.
Coordinate project kickoff meetings internally and with customers when required.
Ensure work orders and project activities are planned and scheduled appropriately.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

Serve as the primary point of contact for customers throughout project execution.
Build strong customer relationships and ensure consistent communication and project updates.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders including Sales, Tendering, Operations, Supply Chain, Technical Support, and Service teams.
Manage third-party vendors and partners involved in project delivery.

Financial & Contract Management

Own project profitability, including revenue, margin, cost control, cash flow, forecasting, and billing milestones.
Monitor project spending against budget and identify opportunities to improve gross margin.
Review contractual obligations and manage project changes, claims, and variation orders.
Support timely invoicing and collection activities to ensure healthy project cash flow.

Risk, Quality & Compliance

Ensure the highest standards of safety throughout project execution.
Identify risks, develop mitigation plans, and proactively address project issues.
Lead issue resolution activities and escalate concerns when necessary.
Maintain compliance with contractual, statutory, and company requirements.
Drive continuous improvement through lessons learned and project reviews.

Project Closeout

Ensure successful project completion, documentation, and formal project closure.
Archive project records and share key learnings with relevant stakeholders.
Support forecasting and planning activities for upcoming projects.

What Qualifications Will Make You Successful?

Education

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Project Management, or a related discipline.

Experience & Technical Knowledge

Experience managing customer-facing projects in field services, electrical systems, industrial automation, energy management, or related industries.
Knowledge of Medium Voltage and Low Voltage distribution solutions, UPS systems, cooling solutions, or similar technical offerings.
Strong understanding of project management principles, methodologies, and best practices.
Proficiency with project management and reporting tools, including Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Project.

Skills

Excellent leadership and stakeholder management skills.
Strong negotiation, conflict resolution, and change management capabilities.
Effective planning, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
Strong financial and commercial acumen.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Customer-focused mindset with excellent communication skills
English proficiency is required for this position due to the need to regularly communicate and collaborate with stakeholders, business partners, customers, and teams located outside Quebec. Bilingualism (English and French) is considered an asset.

You'll have the opportunity to lead impactful customer projects, collaborate with diverse teams, influence business performance, and contribute to delivering innovative service solutions that create value for customers and the organization.

Contract Review

new_jobs.description:
About Us

One team. Global challenges. Infinite opportunities. At Viasat, we’re on a mission to deliver connections with the capacity to change the world. For more than 35 years, Viasat has helped shape how consumers, businesses, governments and militaries around the globe communicate. We’re looking for people who think big, act fearlessly, and create an inclusive environment that drives positive impact to join our team.

What You'll Do

We are thrilled to announce an opening for an Operations Program Manager to join our dynamic VGOV Aviation team in Duluth, GA!

The Operations Program Manager (OPM) leads multi-functional production and aftermarket program teams and acts as the single point of accountability. They are a critical bridge between engineering, operations, and the business area to ensure the seamless transition of innovative products from concept through launch and sustainment. They focus on delivering world-class, high-visibility products on time, at scale, and of the highest quality. This role is a unique and rewarding position, combining aspects of production manufacturing, product engineering, depot repair, material control, and program management. Qualified candidates who are results driven, problem solvers, good communicators, and work well in a team-oriented environment should apply.

The day-to-day

You will apply your excellent leadership skills and your operations, engineering, and supply chain knowledge. You will ensure the cross-functional team meets business objectives and improves processes continuously. Your core responsibilities will consist of the following:

Cross functional leadership: Provides day-to-day direction to a multi-functional team including representatives from manufacturing, test engineering, sourcing, production planning, and quality assurance.
Leads and directs regular core team meetings while attending and reporting at executive program business reviews. Translates product line forecasts into an operational build plan. Manages schedule and product updates or adjustments. Plans labor forecasting and manufacturing capacity. Completes essential performance metrics.
On Time Delivery: Ensure we are building/delivering and repairing/returning to our contractual commitments on our customer’s behalf.
Budget Execution: Responsible for defined budgets that must be well controlled to ensure program profitability.
Continuous Improvement: Identifies opportunities to apply lean methodologies to our production manufacturing and repair stations aimed at improving throughput, cost, and quality that are inclusive of up and downstream operations.
Product Lifecycle Management: Responsible for overseeing the entire PLM including production readiness, production execution, product updates & engineering change orders, obsolescence management, and aftermarket sustainment.

What You'll Need

4+ of experience in roles such as program management, operations management, or engineering (a mix of these in a hardware focused environment is highly preferred).
Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain & Operations, Engineering, or equivalent experience.
Proficiency in ERP systems (Oracle, SAP, or similar); advanced Excel skills for data analysis; ability to influence multi-functional teams via outstanding communications skills.
US Citizenship is required.
Must be able to work onsite in our Duluth, GA office 3 days a week minimum

What Will Help You On The Job

Familiarity with aerospace products or RF components is a significant plus. Ability to partner with engineering to influence product design, focusing on manufacturability, testability, cost, and scalability.
You don’t need a roadmap; you build one. You are comfortable making decisions, taking ownership, and driving projects forward with minimal supervision.
Data-Driven Approach: You enjoy digging into data to find patterns and continuous improvement opportunities.
Financial Literacy: You are experienced with managing budgets and are aware of operational levers and methods that ensure financial success.
Risk Management: Experience with identifying risks and generating recovery plans.
Complete Under Pressure: Proven ability to work under pressure, navigate ambiguity, and consistently deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
Certifications: PMP, CSCP, CPIM, Lean Six Sigma Green Belt (or higher)

Salary range

$120,500.00 - $190,000.00 / annually. For specific work locations within San Jose, the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, the base pay range for this role is $149,500.00- $224,500.00/ annually

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - Digital Twin
new_jobs.description:
Overview

We are seeking a Senior Manager for the Technical Program Management (TPM) of Digital Twin program in Supply Chain. The TPM for Digital Twin will partner closely with Digital Twin Leadership, Product Owners, Enterprise Architects, Solution Architects, other cross-functional capability teams and external partners to deliver Digital Twin applications through global solutions. The role will be accountable for product delivery (BuildOps) governance and execution oversight throughout the product lifecycle from ideation and discovery through implementation and support.

This leader will bring strong delivery mindset and will work closely with internal and external stakeholders to deliver Digital Twin capabilities across PepsiCo facilities globally including but not limited to Manufacturing plants, warehouses, and yards.

Responsibilities

Lead Global BuildOps (project execution and delivery) with cross-functional mission-based teams across IT/OT, Data & AI, Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, and Sector IT
Drive end-to-end technical program management from initial conception, through design and development, to delivery of tested, useable prototypes and final applications
Collaborate with cross-functional partners (Product, engineering, business, design, architecture and external partners) to identify scope, constraints, dependencies, risks, and timelines across programs
Establish a consistent and scalable delivery methodology with all stakeholders
Lead the complex transformation program by guiding partners on PepsiCo-specific tools, frameworks, and processes related to Project Planning and DevSecOps Delivery
Proactively identify technical, procedural, legal, logistical, budget, and communications challenges and partner with leads to drive creative solutions to resolve issues and mitigate risks
Coordinate communications across internal and external teams, including upwards communication to team leadership
Communicate frequently with program leadership to shape and deliver on the product roadmap, and nimbly switch between strategic and tactical initiatives to achieve technical and business objectives within the schedule and budget
Create detailed Project Plans through PI Planning sessions and provide day-to-day governance to execute the project based on that plan
Partner with strategic vendors and system integrators to deliver against roadmap with measurable milestones, quality standards, and cost discipline
Provide timely reporting and necessary escalations to leadership teams and present in regular reporting cadences including BuildOps Reviews, ART syncs and SteerCo meetings
Establish guidelines and conduct stage gates to ensure project milestones are exited with acceptable quality standards, applicable security protocols and functional completion of the digital application

Compensation & Benefits:

The expected compensation range for this position is between $140,100 - $234,850.
Location, confirmed job-related skills, experience, and education will be considered in setting actual starting salary. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range during the hiring process.
Bonus based on performance and eligibility target payout is 15% of annual salary paid out annually.
Paid time off subject to eligibility, including paid parental leave, vacation, sick, and bereavement.
In addition to salary, PepsiCo offers a comprehensive benefits package to support our employees and their families, subject to elections and eligibility: Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Health, and Dependent Care Reimbursement Accounts, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Insurance (Accident, Group Legal, Life), Defined Contribution Retirement Plan.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred in Engineering, Computer Science, IT, Supply Chain, Data/Analytics, or a comparable field.

Experience:

The ideal Technical Program Manager (TPM) will have 8-10 years of work experience, with 3-5 years of experience as Delivery Lead / Technical Program Manager leading delivery of complex digital transformation projects
They will be highly quantitative, have great judgment, able to connect the dots across workstreams, identify critical program dependencies, and have a strong track record of delivery
They will have a pragmatic outlook and iterative approach to building technical solutions including ability to simplify and get things done with a demonstrated track record of working effectively with external and internal teams
They will dive deep to understand the program including the infrastructure, dataset dependencies for local requirements for feature/application deployments, and integration testing requirements before deployment
They will bring exceptional business relationship skills including the ability to discover the true requirements underlying feature requests, recommend alternative technical and business approaches, and lead engineering efforts to meet aggressive timelines with optimal solutions
Their strong experience in project delivery using SAFe Agile methodology and familiarity with other delivery models including waterfall is key
They will have good understanding of SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle) models and a track record of shipping software efficiently along with the ability to recognize the difference between building software and shipping software
They will have strong experience in managing project timelines, budgets and status reports, navigating Change Approval Boards and associated processes. They must be proficient in Azure DevOps (ADO) Boards/Backlogs/Queries along with expertise in entire Microsoft Office 365 suite
They have a proven track record of program delivery for large, cross-functional, projects
They have deep hands-on technical expertise, and excellent verbal and written communication skills
They are familiar with Supply Chain business processes, systems and personas

Leadership:

Executive influence and ability to align business and technology stakeholders globally.
Strong delivery leadership (Product Backlog management, PI Planning, delivery milestones, Stage Gates, Deployment, Hypercare, Reporting & Governance).
Ability to lead high-performing multidisciplinary teams and vendors with high accountability.

Differentiating Qualities:

Demonstrate perseverance and resilience in the pursuit of goals. Confront and work to resolve tough issues. Exhibit a “can-do” attitude and a willingness to take on significant challenges
Demonstrate a sense of passion, enjoyment, and pride in their work. Demonstrate a positive attitude in the workplace. Embrace and adapt well to change. Create a work environment that makes work rewarding and enjoyable
Build convincing, persuasive, and logical storyboards. Have a strong executive presence. Able to communicate effectively and succinctly, both verbally and on paper
Analyze complex problems quickly to find actionable, pragmatic solutions. See connections in data, events, trends, etc. Consistently work based on the right priorities

You understand the systems in your product or program space, their limitations, scaling factors, boundary conditions, and reasons behind architectural choices.

We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!

Coordinate the design, development, testing and deployment of features into production across multiple technical teams.
Create and track project milestones, risks and dependencies, describe, own and prioritize all technical requirements associated with delivery.
Dive deep and understand the design details of the systems in your area, especially those related to customer interfaces, and the expectations for system dependencies.

Develop an implementation plan across teams.
Demonstrate good judgment in how and when to escalate critical program decisions.
Write effective narratives on program decisions, technical trade-offs and program updates.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
5+ years of working directly with engineering teams in product management, program management or engineering roles
3+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams, platform development teams or technology operations.
Experience managing programs across technical and business teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules.
Ability to earn trust, maintain positive and professional relationships, and contribute to a culture of inclusion.
Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience defining KPI's/SLAs used to drive technology delivery and product health.
Proven track record of delivering results for technology project delivery across technical teams and business users.
Experience with Confluence, JIRA
Experience with data analysis to capture, process, and organize data to uncover actionable insights.

Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Overview

Saronic Technologies is seeking a Program Manager of Mission Package Integration to lead the development, integration, and delivery of modules, kits, and mission packages onto Saronic’s growing portfolio of Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) programs.

The Mission Package Integrations PM is a technical executor focusing on bridging Saronic platforms with both bespoke and commercial off the shelf kits, modules, and payloads. This role focuses on supporting existing customer contracts, strategizing new product lines, and driving organic growth through Saronic and customer-derived mission packages.

This role partners closely with the Saronic Growth, Programs and Strategic Partnerships organizations. This role is also expected to embed directly into programs, customer engagements, partnerships, or internal initiatives to provide support and technical expertise.

Responsibilities

Technical Execution Leadership

Lead end-to-end technical execution for mission package integration on Saronic platforms, from design support through field deployment and sustainment.
Support complex payload and package integrations on Saronic’s 180ft Marauder, while also supporting Corsair and Mirage integration efforts.
Translate high-level requirements into actionable steps for engineering and operations teams, driving disciplined technical execution in ambiguous environments.
Maintain technical baselines across multiple mission packaged, ensuring traceability from design to delivery.
Drive technical risk identification, mitigation, and resolution with cross-functional teams.
Contribute to Engineering Change Boards (ECB) and other technical working groups at Saronic

Integration & Field Readiness

Plan and oversee integration, testing, and on-water operations in coordination with Product, Engineering, and Production.
Provide clear technical direction and coordination for cross-functional teams during field trials, demonstrations, and acceptance events.
Ensure technical configurations are validated and approved before production and deployment.
Capture and communicate lessons learned from test events and field operations into future iterations.

Cross Functional Coordination

Work closely with engineering, software, forward deployed engineering, mission operations, and product teams to synchronize integration schedules and milestones.
Coordinate with Engineering to ensure scope, design intent, and technical priorities are aligned with program goals.
Interface with Production and Quality to ensure build configurations and acceptance criteria meet customer expectations.
Support Program Managers with technical inputs for customer meetings, reporting, and deliverables.

Risk & Configuration Management

Maintain visibility into technical, operational, and programmatic risks across assigned packages.
Lead risk review meetings and maintain mitigation plans in collaboration with Program, Product, and Engineering leadership.
Enforce disciplined configuration management for vessels, payloads, and software versions.
Oversee technical documentation, ensuring completeness, traceability, and readiness for audits or delivery.

Serve as a dynamic point of contact for technical customer engagements, bridging operational needs with package capability.
Participate in design reviews, field demos, and technical exchanges with customer stakeholders.
Deliver concise technical updates and after action reports to leadership and customer audiences.
Translate real-world customer feedback into actionable improvements for Product and Engineering.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Naval Architecture, or a related technical field.
5+ years of experience in technical program management, systems integration, or defense-related development programs.
Demonstrated success leading cross-functional technical teams through the design, build, and integration lifecycle.
Strong understanding of mechanical, electrical, software, and autonomy integration principles.
Proven experience managing risk, configuration, and readiness for complex technical maritime systems.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interface confidently with technical and non-technical audiences.
Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time.
Secret security clearance eligibility required, active preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing or integrating unmanned defense, maritime, or robotic systems.
Familiarity with naval readiness systems and logistics management systems.
Experience building or supporting sustainment and training infrastructures for new technologies.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment with a strong growth mandate.

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Occasional standing and walking within the office
Manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment
Visual acuity to read screens, documents, and reports
Occasional reaching, bending, or stooping to access file drawers, cabinets, or office supplies
Lifting and carrying items up to 20 pounds occasionally (e.g., office supplies, packages)

Key Competencies

Can connect component-level design decisions to overall system and mission performance.
Can translate complex technical data into clear, actionable information for stakeholders.
Leadership of high performing distributed technical teams.
Ability to balance execution excellence with growth, team-building, and organizational scaling.
Established track record of clear, consistent, and correct communications with peers, leaders, and external stakeholders.
Comfort guiding customers through ambiguous or evolving requirements and shaping actionable solutions.

Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

Serve as escalation point for complex in-flight technical issues; engage hands-on when warranted while ensuring the team learns from every resolution.
Champion Zero Trust and SASE architecture principles within ECI’s implementation workflows.

Client & Stakeholder Communication

Own implementation status communication to client stakeholders; translate technical risk into clear business impact language.
Represent the implementation team in internal delivery reviews, capacity planning, and service improvement forums.
Maintain ECI’s documentation standard across implementation plans, network diagrams, as-built records, and configuration baselines — ensuring clean handoffs to managed services teams.

Qualifications

Required

10+ years of progressive network engineering experience with a demonstrable track record in enterprise implementation, ideally within an MSP or multi-client environment.
3+ years of direct people management — you have hired engineers, set goals, handled performance, and actively developed talent.
Deep technical proficiency in Cisco networking (Catalyst, Nexus, IOS-XE/XR), Palo Alto firewalls (App-ID, Threat Prevention, VPN, Panorama), and wireless (WLC, Meraki MR/MS/MX).
Strong working knowledge of routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, EIGRP), VLANs, QoS, and IPv4/IPv6 fundamentals.
Proven ability to run multiple concurrent implementation projects with accountability for schedules, resources, and stakeholder communication.
Solid understanding of security frameworks, compliance standards, and change management governance in regulated client environments.

Preferred

Active CCNP, CCIE, or PCNSE certification; equivalent demonstrated expertise considered.
Experience with SD-WAN (Cisco Viptela, VeloCloud) and SASE / Zero Trust architecture in client deployments.
Familiarity with automation tooling (Python, Ansible) to drive repeatability and reduce manual effort across the team.
Experience with network monitoring platforms (SolarWinds, PRTG, Meraki Insights) and using telemetry data to drive delivery quality.
Hedge fund, financial services, or similarly regulated client-facing environment experience is a strong plus.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field — or equivalent professional experience.
