Beyond credentials, we are hiring for a specific leadership profile. The right candidate:

Communicates expectations without ambiguity and follows through consistently. Leads with clarity.
Engineers respect them because they know the stack — not just the title. Commands technical credibility.
Holds the team and themselves to high execution standards without micromanaging. Drives accountability.
Focused on delivery quality and reliability, not just activity volume. Solves for client outcomes.
Understands the job is to build the best team — not to be the best individual engineer on it. Scales through people.

Job Description

Description reviewed 08/18/26

Basic Purpose

Positions in this job family are assigned responsibility involving the coordination, supervision and direction of a correctional security program in a state adult correctional facility.

Typical Functions

Coordinates and supervises or directs correctional security functions and activities at an adult correctional facility; may serve as a shift supervisor with responsibility for all assigned units and functions in a large facility or as the chief of security in a smaller facility.
May serve as commander of a correctional emergency response team; schedules training exercises and coordinates activities.
Conducts special investigations, particularly concerning incidents that occur during assigned shifts.
Coordinates and supervises security, riot and escape procedures, including procedures for inmate counts and searches for escape materials and contraband.
Prepares daily work schedules for security personnel; prepares and maintains appropriate records concerning employees and residents.
Conducts inspections of assigned staff at beginning of shift to assure proper attire and fitness for duty; makes periodic inspections of posts to assure that they are properly maintained; prepares administrative reports concerning the operation of the shift.
Acts as liaison to local law enforcement agencies; provides information and file changes; arranges court appearances.
Serves as member of the administrative institutional staff; participates in the formulation of institutional policies, rules and regulations.

Level Descriptor

At this level employees serve as a correctional security captain with overall responsibility for the operations of an assigned shift within a medium or maximum-security facility and supervision of staff.

Responsibilities may involve ensuring the proper functioning of the electronic, mechanical, surveillance, and physical security systems; overseeing physical and sanitary conditions, special investigations, and adherence to operational and policy protocols; directing the correctional emergency response team; and assumption of the operation and management of the facility after normal business hours or in the absence of the warden.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, And Competencies

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities required at this level include knowledge of supervisory methods and techniques; of staffing patterns and scheduling the distribution of staff and work assignments; of methods and objectives of discipline required for inmates under restraint; of the psychology of inmate behavior; of the use and care of firearms; of proper restraint methods and techniques; of the fundamentals of English usage; of basic math; of report writing techniques; and of the modern practices of prison management

and the treatment of inmates.

Ability is required to establish and maintain effective working relationships; to follow oral and written instructions; to gather and organize facts and complete clear, concise reports; to quickly evaluate a situation and adopt an effective course of action; to exercise alertness and be able to act quickly in an emergency; to effectively communicate security techniques; to maintain proficiency in firearms; to assess and manage conflict resolutions within the inmate population; and to direct and supervise the work of others.

Education And Experience

Education and Experience requirements at this level consist of four years of experience in correctional or security work for a government agency or private corrections agency and the following statutory requirements of Title 57, O.S. Section 510: a. The minimum age for service shall be twenty (20) years of age. The Director shall have the authority to establish the maximum age for correctional officers entering service and b. possession of thirty (30) semester hours from an accredited college or university; or possession of a high school diploma acquired from an accredited high school or GED equivalent testing program and graduation from a training course conducted by or approved by the Department and certified by the Council on Law Enforcement Education and Training either prior to employment or during the first six (6) months of employment.

Note: Successful completion of the GED test is based upon standards established by the Oklahoma Department of Education.

Special Requirements

Per 57 O.S. 510 applicants/employees in this job family shall be subject to the following additional requirements: (a) be of good moral character; (b) before going on duty alone, satisfactory completion of an adequate training program for correctional officers and guards, as prescribed and approved by the State Board of Corrections; and (c) satisfactory completion of a physical in keeping with the conditions of the job description on an annual basis and along the guidelines as established by the Department of Corrections.

Applicants must possess a valid driver’s license at the time of appointment in order to perform necessary travel.

Applicants will be subject to drug testing.

Applicants must be willing and able to work any assigned shift or day of the week.

NOTE: Employees in this job classification may be designated as peace officers by the Director and required to meet the training and screening requirements conducted by the Department and certified by the Council on Law Enforcement Education and Training. (57 O.S. 510)

No person who has received a verdict of guilty or pled guilty or nolo contendere to any offense required to register pursuant to the Sex Offenders Registration Act is eligible for employment as a peace officer. (57 O.S. 589.C)

No person who has been convicted of a crime of moral turpitude who has not received a full pardon from the proper agency is eligible for employment as a peace officer. (70 O.S. 3311)

No person who has been convicted of a nonviolent felony and who has not received a full pardon from the proper authority, or who has been convicted of any other felony offense, is eligible for employment in this job classification. (21 O.S. 1283.B)

No person who has been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence, who has not been pardoned for, or had the conviction expunged or set aside, or is subject to a court order that restrains the person from harassing, stalking, or threatening an intimate partner or the partners’ child or engaging in other conduct that would place an intimate partner or the partners’ child in reasonable fear of bodily injury

and includes a finding that the person is a credible threat; or who has been dishonorably discharged from any branch of the armed services is eligible for employment in this job classification. (18 U.S.C. 922)

Under the general direction of the Senior Program Manager of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Programs or designee, the SNAP Program Manager provides leadership and operational oversight of the SNAP Employment and Training (known in Massachusetts as SNAP Path to Work) team within ForHealth Consulting. This role is responsible for managing staff and coordinating SNAP team activities, including partner recruitment and training, budget development, federal and state claiming processes, performance monitoring, and general departmental operations. The position is tasked with leading initiatives that advance ForHealth Consultings SNAP portfolio.

The successful candidate for this position will demonstrate operational management expertise, a strong aptitude for creative problem-solving, a commitment to implementing process improvements and innovative practices, and a comfort level with budgeting and financial decision-making. Exceptional organizational and leadership skills are essential, as the SNAP program manager must handle multiple assignments with minimal supervision and effectively collaborate with diverse internal and external partners. This position may require occasional travel to locations within Massachusetts and elsewhere in New England.

The Access and Eligibility Services (AES) group is part of ForHealth Consulting, a division of UMass Chan Medical School. AES supports critical state and federal public assistance programs on behalf of the Massachusetts Department of Transitional Assistance (DTA) to help hundreds of thousands of low-income individuals in Massachusetts with food and shelter expenses. ForHealth Consulting contracts with community organizations and agencies who provide services to DTA SNAP clients and applicants. SNAP Path to Work is a program that connects SNAP clients in Massachusetts with community providers of job skills training programs and employment preparation. The SNAP team at ForHealth Consulting assists DTAs SNAP community partners to obtain federal dollars for eligible services under the SNAP Path to Work and Outreach programs by identifying allowable activities and funding streams, offering training and technical assistance, reviewing quarterly claims, and disbursing federal reimbursements.

Responsibilities

Provide supplemental support to the SNAP Senior Program Manager; manage general operations of the unit to meet client goals and expectations. Ensure appropriate staffing levels and timely completion of all projects and tasks.
Oversee and manage staff activities related to preparing and completing federal claims and monitoring contracted partners. Review claims for accuracy and compliance and/or authorize claims for submission.
Manage the work of the SNAP team to complete annual partner reviews and audits, including partner budget reviews.
Assist in preparing operational budgets for the SNAP unit.
Help develop, implement, and recommend improvements to SNAP programs to expand the partner base, increase federal claiming, and optimize outcomes for community partners. Develop and implement procedures and guidelines to accomplish project objectives and goals efficiently.
Ensure that all activities of the SNAP unit and its policies and procedures for partners are compliant with applicable state and federal rules and regulations.
Lead strategic recruitment efforts of new partners to address community and client needs.
Collaborate with staff and support units to ensure timely and accurate financial reconciliation for SNAP-related activities.
Manage staff and conduct annual performance reviews to ensure alignment with organizational goals and to foster individual growth and professional development.
Foster a culture of innovation and continuous improvement among SNAP staff through regular meetings, ongoing awareness and support for new ideas.
Represent the department in a professional capacity with internal management, contracted partners, DTA leadership, and other government agencies.
Participate in the broader AES team and support its programs and projects where necessary.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Finance, Fiscal Management, or a related field, or two years of relevant professional experience in lieu of the degree.
Demonstrated strong experience in supervision with the ability to manage and motivate staff
Proficiency in computer-based tools, including spreadsheets and word processing software (MS Office Suite)

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of state and federal regulations as they apply to public assistance programs
Understanding of SNAP regulations related to SNAP Employment and Training (SNAP Path to Work), strongly preferred
Knowledge of United States Department of Agriculture Food and Nutrition Administration (USDA FNA) programs and/or experience working with the advocate community on nutrition and anti-hunger projects
Experience in financial or operational management, including fiscal responsibility and decision-making
Strong oral and written communication skills

We combine advanced business management technology with personalized consulting to provide unmatched scale, efficiency, and support. Our advisor-focused culture is built on innovation and advocacy, enabling advisors to offer comprehensive securities and investment advisory solutions to their clients

Lead with Purpose. Partner with Impact

Kestra Financial, a leading provider of wealth management platforms, technology solutions, and investment products empowering independent financial advisors and RIAs nationwide, is seeking a Senior Strategic Implementation Manager.

This role serves as a pivotal execution leader accountable for the disciplined delivery of Kestra Wealth Management’s highest-priority strategic initiatives in investment products and platform capabilities. You will drive the successful launch of new investment products and manage end-to-end launch campaigns while coordinating complex cross-functional projects spanning technology, compliance, business development, and operations.

By implementing and championing agile, Scrum-like cadences and robust portfolio governance practices, you will build transparency, predictability, and accountability across initiatives. Your leadership will ensure that strategic intent translates into measurable business outcomes—including accelerated advisor adoption, revenue contribution from new products, enhanced platform capabilities, and operational excellence.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for a collaborative leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, execution, and cross-functional influence in a dynamic, growth-oriented wealth management environment.

What You’ll Do:

Own the end-to-end governance and planning that results in successful delivery of priority investment product launches (e.g., alternative investment solutions, insurance products, or curated offerings) and strategic platform implementation initiatives (new advisory revenue vertical, investment program redesign, etc) from concept through post-launch optimization and benefits realization.
Lead the coordination and execution of comprehensive launch campaigns, aligning go-to-market activities including sales enablement, marketing communications, advisor training and onboarding programs, distribution strategy, and adoption tracking to drive rapid uptake and sustained engagement.
Establish and maintain a prioritized portfolio of strategic initiatives for Investment Platforms & Products; drive rigorous sequencing, capacity alignment, funding discipline, and proactive trade-off decisions (scope, timeline, resources, investment) aligned to Kestra’s business objectives and growth priorities.
Partner with Product Management to translate product strategy and roadmap into executable implementation plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and success criteria.
Support Wealth Management platform and product leads by facilitating high-performing cross-functional project teams and workstreams involving:
Technology: Platform development, data integrations (including MDM/medallion architectures), APIs, advisor portals/tools, and infrastructure enhancements.
Compliance & Legal: Product due diligence, regulatory reviews/approvals, disclosures, risk assessments, and ongoing product governance to ensure adherence to SEC, FINRA, fiduciary, and other requirements.
Business: Commercialization strategy, RIA/advisor engagement and feedback loops, distribution channel readiness, pricing/packaging, and P&L impact modeling.
Operations & Finance: Operational readiness, process design, financial tracking, and benefits measurement.
Map and manage complex dependencies, risks, and interdependencies across teams; proactively identify and remove blockers while fostering alignment and shared ownership in a matrixed environment.
Ensure every initiative incorporates appropriate compliance guardrails, risk controls, audit readiness, and change management from the start.
Design, implement, and continuously mature agile delivery operating models tailored to regulated investment product and platform initiatives. This includes establishing Scrum-like cadences (sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives), Kanban for workflow transparency and flow optimization, and scaled frameworks (e.g., program-level planning or release management) for larger or interdependent efforts.
Stand up consistent governance rhythms and forums, including steering committees, launch readiness reviews/tollgates, dependency management sessions, risk reviews, and clear escalation paths to executive leadership.
Drive adoption of modern agile/project tools (Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or equivalent) and best practices to improve delivery velocity, predictability, collaboration, and quality across technology and business teams.
Champion a shift toward iterative, outcome-focused delivery—balancing the need for structure and compliance in product launches with the speed and adaptability required in a competitive wealth tech landscape.
Build and operate a portfolio “control tower” capability: deliver timely, credible, decision-oriented reporting and dashboards on initiative status, milestones, risks/issues, dependencies, financial performance (budget vs. plan, ROI tracking), and leading indicators of business impact.
Define, track, and report on key business outcome metrics tied to each strategic initiative (e.g., new product net flows/AUM/revenue contribution, advisor adoption and usage rates, client/advisor satisfaction or NPS impact, reduction in time-to-market or launch cycle time, compliance adherence, platform feature utilization and engagement).
Proactively surface execution risks, capacity constraints, and recommended trade-offs to senior leadership; lead structured issue resolution, corrective action planning, and recovery efforts to protect delivery commitments and protect/enhance business results.
Prepare and present high-quality materials for executive leadership, steering committees, and governance forums; represent the delivery health and outlook of the Investment Platforms & Products portfolio with clarity and fact-based insights.
Instill a culture of genuine accountability—where teams own and are measured on the delivery of agreed business outcomes and value realization, not merely activity completion or milestone hitting.

What You Bring:

2+ years experience in technical product management in an Agile environment.
5+ years of experience in wealth management, investment operations, or trading
3-5+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic program/portfolio management, product implementation, launch execution, or enterprise transformation roles within wealth management, RIA platforms, investment product development, fintech, asset/wealth platforms, or similarly complex, regulated financial services environments.

new_jobs.description:
MTSI is seeking a Senior Operations Analyst & Field Lead
to support a key joint development program delivering advanced warfighting tools, technologies, and operational integration across the Department of Defense. The role blends senior-level operational expertise with hands-on field support, operator training, system troubleshooting, and technology transition activities. The individual will serve as a primary operational and technical interface between development teams, program leadership, and warfighters throughout daily operations, fielding events, and constructive, virtual, and live exercises. The selected candidate will sit at Offutt Air Force Base.

Responsibilities

Provide senior military operations analysis and subject matter expertise in one or more warfare areas or domains. Analyze U.S. and adversary concepts of operations, tactics, techniques, and procedures to inform system development, capability assessment, and operational employment.
Serve as a technical and operational advisor to program managers, development teams, and DoD stakeholders for the evaluation, transition, and fielding of advanced warfighting tools and technologies.
Assess how emerging systems and software capabilities support military operations, command and control processes, fires execution, and current or future Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures.
Provide on-site operational and technical support during daily operations, exercises, demonstrations, integration events, and field experimentation.
Train operators and military staff on advanced warfighting software, hardware, and supporting systems to ensure mission readiness and effective operational employment.
Serve as the primary field interface between warfighters, technical program managers, software developers, and system engineers.
Support system configuration, operator workflow development, and user adoption during technology transition and fielding efforts.
Provide real-time troubleshooting during operational use, exercises, demonstrations, and experimentation events.
Coordinate with technical experts, software developers, and system engineers to resolve hardware, software, network, and configuration issues.
Support routine maintenance, emergency troubleshooting, and sustainment activities to ensure systems remain mission-ready.
Evaluate system performance and operational effectiveness in support of military staff processes and current TTPs.
Identify operational gaps, technical limitations, workflow issues, and opportunities to improve system employment in high-stakes operational environments.

COCOM LNO Duties

Serve as a forward-deployed liaison officer (LNO) to designated Combatant Command or field sites, acting as the program’s on-site representative for operational coordination, user engagement, and system integration.
Facilitate communication between program leadership, warfighters, and technical teams to ensure operational requirements, system issues, and emerging needs are accurately captured and rapidly addressed.
Support planning, execution, and assessment of operational events, readiness activities, experimentation, and technology transition efforts occurring at assigned commands or sites.
Provide day-to-day guidance, troubleshooting, training, and workflow support to operators employing advanced warfighting tools and technologies in real-world or exercise environments.

Required Experience

18+ years of military experience with O-5 command and/or Operational Fleet Staff (3-star) assignments.
Experience supporting or employing advanced joint C2 and fires-related systems such as JFN and/or CJADC2
Operational experience in a warfighting role within one or more warfare areas, with demonstrated proficiency in operational and technical analysis of U.S. and adversary CONOPS and TTPs.
5+ years of experience working in a multi-level security environment.
Experience leading and managing teams to solve complex technical, management, and administrative challenges.
Demonstrated ability to conduct research and analysis using incomplete information, develop clear analytic products, and present results effectively.
Excellent interpersonal communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel).
Strong documentation, writing, and reporting skills.
Must be a self-starter with the ability to take initiative, work independently, and elevate issues appropriately.
Ability to multi-task and maintain deadline punctuality in high-pressure situations.

Required Education

Bachelor's Degree in a technical field of study
Master's Degree preferred

TS/SCI

new_jobs.title: PKI Deputy Contract Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
The PKI Deputy Contract Program Manager will serve as the secondary representative for the Air Force Public Key Infrastructure (AF PKI) Program contract, overseeing all mission support work and ensuring adherence to specified standards. This role involves supporting the Contract Program Manager in maintaining quality assurance and configuration control, implementing a systematic management approach, developing project schedules, and conducting monthly financial reviews with the Government Program Manager (PM). The Deputy Contract Program Manager will help manage functional, capability, and delivery teams within a structured framework, requiring a seasoned leader with expertise in project management, PKI operations, and contract oversight within a Department of the Air Force (DAF) context.

Job Duties

Project Oversight: Act as the secondary representative responsible for overseeing all direct mission support work under the contract, ensuring compliance with all referenced standards and requirements.

Quality and Configuration Control: Maintain quality assurance and configuration control for all products and services provided to and by the AF PKI program, ensuring consistency and reliability.

Management Approach: Implement a systematic management process to support PWS processes and requirements, coordinating functional, integrated capability, and product delivery teams within a controlled structure.

Schedule Development: Provide detailed program/project schedules for tasks and activities outlined in the PWS, ensuring compatibility with Microsoft Project for export and review. Develop a single Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) that will include all activities to sustain the AF PKI, activities supporting DoD PKI implementation, evolution of AF PKI capabilities, and other activities.

Financial Reviews: Meet monthly with the Government PM to review contract funding status, including labor forecast versus actual, cumulative travel costs, and cumulative Other Direct Costs (ODCs), to ensure fiscal accountability.

Continuity of Operations (COOP): Collaborate with the Government to identify AF PKI SPO essential functions and operations requiring uninterrupted availability. Develop, maintain, and test a comprehensive COOP. Deliver the initial COOP to the Government on an agreed date, no later than six months after the contract start date of June 1, 2025.

External Meeting Participation: Ensure team representation in DoD and AF recurring meetings regarding PKI (ex. Summits, Program Information Exchanges, working groups). Ensure preparedness and professional conduct of AF PKI contractor representatives in meetings.

Required Qualifications

Project Management: Proven experience leading complex technical projects, preferably in cybersecurity or PKI programs, with oversight of multiple teams and deliverables.

PKI Knowledge: Familiarity with PKI systems and operations within a DoD or DAF environment, ensuring alignment with program goals.

Quality Assurance: Expertise in maintaining quality assurance and configuration control for technical products and services.

Scheduling Skills: Proficiency in developing and managing project schedules, with experience using Microsoft Project or similar tools.

Financial Oversight: Ability to track and review contract funding, including labor, travel, and ODCs, with strong analytical and reporting skills.

Leadership: Strong ability to coordinate and manage diverse teams within a structured framework, ensuring systematic execution of tasks.

Security Clearance: Must possess or be eligible to obtain and maintain a minimum Secret clearance, with all employees cleared to at least Secret by the contract start date of June 1, 2025.

Location: Ability to work in San Antonio, TX, with potential on-site support at the Government-leased facility for oversight and coordination.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in related field.

Preferred Qualifications

Security Clearance: Active Top Secret (TS) or Top Secret /Secure Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance.

DAF PKI Experience: Prior leadership role in an AF PKI or similar DoD program, providing context for program-specific standards and processes.

Certifications: Relevant certifications such as Project Management Professional (PMP), CompTIA Security+, or DoD 8570/8140-approved Information Assurance certifications (e.g., IAT Level II or higher).

Team Management: Extensive experience managing functional, capability, and delivery teams in a controlled, systematic environment.

Financial Acumen: Background in contract financial management, with a track record of accurate forecasting and cost control.

Communication: Exceptional skills in presenting schedules and financial updates to Government stakeholders, ensuring clarity and alignment.

Overview

Conectando clientes aos mercados – e talentos às oportunidades

Com 4.300 funcionários e mais de 400.000 clientes de varejo e institucionais em mais de 80 escritórios espalhados pelos cinco continentes, somos um fornecedor listado na Fortune 100 e listado na Nasdaq, conectando clientes aos mercados globais – com foco em inovação, conexão humana e fornecendo soluções mundiais produtos e serviços de primeira classe para todos os tipos de investidores.

O candidato deve ter perfil analítico, atenção a detalhes e capacidade de trabalhar sob pressão para assegurar a conformidade regulatória e a excelência operacional.

Connecting clients to markets – and talent to opportunity

With 4,500+ employees and over 300,000 commercial, institutional, payments, and retail clients, we operate from more than 70 offices spread across six continents. As a Fortune 100, Nasdaq-listed provider, we connect clients to the global markets – focusing on innovation, human connection, and providing world-class products and services to all types of investors.

We are looking for a professional to work in the Foreign Exchange Bank Operations area, ensuring accurate analysis and compliance of transactions with the Central Bank of Brazil. The candidate should have an analytical profile, attention to detail, and the ability to work under pressure to guarantee regulatory compliance and operational excellence.

Analisar documentação que respalda a operação para enquadramento conforme regulamentação do Banco Central.

Interagir com clientes esclarecendo dúvidas sobre documentação e procedimentos de câmbio.
Interagir com clientes internos e externos buscando solucionar as pendências;
Elaborar relatórios operacionais.

Engage with internal and external stakeholders to resolve pending issues.
Prepare operational reports.

Conhecimento em regulamentações bancárias (BACEN, CVM, CMN, Febraban).

Conhecimento no sistema Exchange.
